title.zh: 卷二百六十五 列傳第二十四 李昉 呂蒙正 張齊賢 賈黃中
title.en: Volume 265 Biographies 24: Li Fang, Lu Mengzheng, Zhang Qixian, Jia Huangzhong
title.raw: 卷二百六十五 列傳第二十四 李昉 呂蒙正 張齊賢 賈黃中 Volume 265 Biographies 24: Li Fang, Lu Mengzheng, Zhang Qixian, Jia Huangzhong

sentences.zh: 李昉，字明遠，深州饒陽人。

translations.literal: Li Fang, style name Mingyuan, was a man of Raoyang in Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fang, whose style was Mingyuan, came from Raoyang in Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 父起，晉工部郎中、集賢殿直學士。

translations.literal: His father Qi was Director in the Ministry of Works under Jin and Academician-Attendant of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qi had served as Director in the Ministry of Works of Jin and as Academician-Attendant of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 從大父右資善大夫超無子，以昉為後，蔭補齋郎，選授太子校書。

translations.literal: His father's elder uncle, the Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent Chao, had no son; Fang was made his heir, received inherited appointment as Chamberlain's Aide, and by selection was appointed Crown Prince's Proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: His great-uncle on his father's side, the Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent Chao, had no children, so Fang was adopted as his heir; through yin privilege he was made a Chamberlain's Aide, and by examination he was selected as Crown Prince's Proofreader.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐舉進士，為秘書郎。

translations.literal: Under Han in the Qianyou era he passed the jinshi examination and became Secretary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianyou reign of Later Han he earned his jinshi degree and was appointed Secretary Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 宰相馮道引之，與呂端同直弘文館，改右拾遺、集賢殿修撰。

translations.literal: The chief minister Feng Dao introduced him; with Lü Duan he served together in the Hongwen Institute, and he was changed to Right Reminder and Compiler of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Feng Dao brought him forward; he served in the Hongwen Institute alongside Lü Duan, then was promoted to Right Reminder and Compiler of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 周顯德二年，宰相李穀征淮南，昉為記室。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiande under Zhou, Chief Minister Li Gu campaigned in Huainan; Fang served as recorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiande of Later Zhou, when Chief Minister Li Gu marched against Huainan, Fang served on his staff as recorder.

sentences.zh: 世宗覽軍中章奏，愛其辭理明白，已知為昉所作，及見《相國寺文英院集》，乃昉與扈蒙、崔頌、劉袞、竇儼、趙逢及昉弟載所題，益善昉詩而稱賞之曰：「吾久知有此人矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong reviewed memorials from the army, loved their clear reasoning, and already knew they were Fang's work; when he saw the Collected Writings of the Wenyuan Court of Xiangguo Temple, composed by Fang together with Hu Meng, Cui Song, Liu Gun, Dou Yan, Zhao Feng, and Fang's younger brother Zai, he grew still fonder of Fang's poetry and praised him, saying: "I have long known there was such a man.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong read through the army's memorials, admired their lucid argument, and already knew Fang had written them; when he came upon the Collected Writings of the Wenyuan Court of Xiangguo Temple—works by Fang together with Hu Meng, Cui Song, Liu Gun, Dou Yan, Zhao Feng, and Fang's younger brother Zai—he admired Fang's poetry all the more and exclaimed, "I have known of this man for a long time.

sentences.zh: 」師還，擢為主客員外郎、知制誥、集賢殿直學士。

translations.literal: " When the army returned he was promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Receptions, Drafting Secretary, and Academician-Attendant of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: " After the army returned he was promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Receptions, given charge of drafting edicts, and made Academician-Attendant of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 四年，加史館修撰、判館事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was additionally made Compiler of the Historiography Institute and given charge of institute affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was further appointed Compiler of the Historiography Institute and put in charge of its affairs.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，世宗南征，從至高郵，會陶穀出使，內署書詔填委，乃命為屯田郎中、翰林學士。

translations.literal: That winter the emperor marched south; Fang followed as far as Gaoyou; when Tao Gu went on embassy, the inner secretariat was piled with edicts, and he was ordered to be Director of the Bureau of State Farms and Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when the emperor campaigned south, Fang accompanied him as far as Gaoyou; Tao Gu was sent abroad on a mission, and with edicts flooding the inner secretariat Fang was appointed Director of the Bureau of State Farms and Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 六年春，丁內艱。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year he observed mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 恭帝嗣位，賜金紫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong succeeded to the throne, he was granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong took the throne, Fang was awarded the gold-and-purple insignia of high office.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was made Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song dynasty he was promoted to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，罷為給事中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong he was dismissed to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianlong he was demoted to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 四年，平湖湘，受詔祀南嶽，就命知衡州，逾年代歸。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he pacified Hunan, received an edict to sacrifice at the Southern Marchmount, and on the spot was ordered to govern Hengzhou; after more than a year he returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, after pacifying Hunan, he received orders to perform sacrifices at the Southern Marchmount and was appointed on the spot to govern Hengzhou; he returned home after a year in office.

sentences.zh: 陶穀誣奏昉為所親求京畿令，上怒，召吏部尚書張昭面質其事。

translations.literal: Tao Gu falsely memorialized that Fang had sought a metropolitan magistracy for a favorite; the emperor was angry and summoned Minister of Personnel Zhang Zhao to confront him face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Gu lodged a false accusation that Fang had sought a capital-district magistracy for a protégé; the emperor was furious and summoned Minister of Personnel Zhang Zhao to question him in person.

sentences.zh: 昭老儒氣直，免冠上前，抗聲云：「穀罔上。

translations.literal: Zhao, an old Confucian of upright spirit, removed his cap and stepped forward, protesting loudly: "Gu has deceived Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, an old scholar of blunt integrity, doffed his cap and stepped forward, declaring in a ringing voice, "Gu has deceived Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」上疑之不釋，出昉為彰武軍行軍司馬，居延州，為生業以老。

translations.literal: " The emperor's doubts were not dispelled; Fang was sent out as Military Administrator of the Zhangwu Army, residing at Yanzhou, where he made a living in his old age.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's suspicions did not lift; Fang was sent out as Military Administrator of the Zhangwu Army and lived at Yanzhou, supporting himself in retirement.

sentences.zh: 三歲當內徙，昉不願。

translations.literal: At three years he should have been transferred inward, but Fang did not wish it.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he was due for an inward transfer, but Fang declined.

sentences.zh: 宰相薦其可大用，開寶二年，召還，復拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: The chief minister recommended that he could be greatly employed; in the second year of Kaibao he was recalled and again appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister recommended him as fit for greater use; in the second year of Kaibao he was recalled and again made Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 未幾，直學士院。

translations.literal: Before long he served in the Academy of Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was assigned to the Academy of Scholars.

sentences.zh: 三年，知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the third year he supervised the civil examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was put in charge of the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 五年，復知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again supervised the civil examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he again oversaw the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 秋，預宴大明殿，上見昉坐盧多遜下，因問宰相，對曰：「多遜學士，昉直殿爾。

translations.literal: In autumn, at a feast in the Hall of Great Brightness, the emperor saw Fang seated below Lu Duosun and therefore asked the chief minister, who replied: "Duosun is an academician; Fang merely attends the hall.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, at a banquet in the Hall of Great Brightness, the emperor noticed Fang seated below Lu Duosun and asked the chief minister why; the reply was, "Duosun is a full academician; Fang only attends the hall.

sentences.zh: 」即令真拜學士，令居多遜上。

translations.literal: " He at once ordered Fang formally appointed academician and seated above Duosun.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor immediately ordered Fang formally invested as academician and given the seat above Duosun.

sentences.zh: 昉之知貢舉也，其鄉人武濟川預選，既而奏對失次，昉坐左遷太常少卿，俄判國子監。

translations.literal: When Fang supervised the examinations, his fellow townsman Wu Jichuan was among the candidates; afterward in palace audience he lost his composure, and Fang was demoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and soon given charge of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang ran the examinations, his fellow townsman Wu Jichuan was among the candidates; later, in a palace audience, Wu lost his composure, and Fang was demoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and soon put in charge of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，復拜中書舍人、翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the next year he was again appointed Secretariat Drafter and Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: The following May he was again made Secretariat Drafter and Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 冬，判吏部銓。

translations.literal: In winter he was given charge of personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was assigned to oversee personnel selection at the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時趙普為多遜所構，數以其短聞於上，上詢於昉，對曰：「臣職司書詔，普之所為，非臣所知。

translations.literal: At the time Zhao Pu was framed by Duosun, who several times reported his faults to the emperor; the emperor inquired of Fang, who replied: "Your servant's duty is drafting edicts; what Pu has done is not known to your servant.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhao Pu was undermined by Duosun, who repeatedly reported his shortcomings to the throne; when the emperor asked Fang, he answered, "My office is to draft edicts; I do not know what Pu has done.

sentences.zh: 」普尋出鎮，多遜遂參知政事。

translations.literal: " Before long Pu went out to command a circuit, and Duosun then became Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long Pu was sent out to govern a military circuit, and Duosun was made Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 雍熙元年郊祀，命昉與琪並為左右僕射，昉固辭，乃加中書侍郎。

translations.literal: At the suburban sacrifice in the first year of Yongxi, Fang and Qi were both ordered as Left and Right Vice Directors, but Fang firmly declined and was instead made Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yongxi suburban sacrifice, Fang and Qi were both named Left and Right Vice Directors, but Fang firmly declined and was made Vice Director of the Secretariat instead.

sentences.zh: 王師討幽薊不利，遣使分詣河南、東，籍民為兵，凡八丁取一。

translations.literal: The imperial army's campaign against You and Ji went badly; envoys were sent to Henan and the east to register the people for military service, taking one man from every eight households.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign against You and Ji faltered; the court sent envoys to Henan and the eastern circuits to register civilians for military service, drafting one man from every eight households.

sentences.zh: 昉等相率奏曰：「近者分遣使籍河南、東四十餘郡之民以為邊備，非得已也。

translations.literal: Fang and others jointly memorialized: "Recently envoys were sent to register the people of more than forty commanderies of Henan and the east for frontier defense—this was not done willingly.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and his colleagues jointly submitted: "Envoys have lately been sent to register the people of more than forty prefectures in Henan and the east for frontier defense—this was not undertaken lightly.

sentences.zh: 然河南之民素習農桑，罔知戰鬥，一旦括集，必致動搖，若因而嘯聚，更須剪除。

translations.literal: Yet the people of Henan are long accustomed to farming and mulberry culture and know nothing of battle; once they are rounded up, disturbance is sure to follow; if they then gather in revolt, further suppression will be needed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the people of Henan have long lived by farming and sericulture and know nothing of war; once they are conscripted en masse, unrest is inevitable, and if they rise in bands, the court will have to suppress them again.

sentences.zh: 如此，則河北閭閻既困於戎馬，河南生聚復擾於萑蒲，矧當春和，有妨農作。

translations.literal: Thus the villages of Hebei will already be worn down by war-horses, and the living masses of Henan will again be harried by brambles and reeds; moreover it is spring, when farming ought not be hindered.
translations.idiomatic: In that case the hamlets of Hebei will already be exhausted by war, and the households of Henan will again be ravaged by rebellion; besides, spring is here, and the farming season must not be disrupted.

sentences.zh: 陛下若以明詔既頒，難於反汗，則當續遣使臣，嚴加戒飭，所至點募，人情若有不安，即須少緩，密奏取裁，庶免後患。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty finds it hard to withdraw a decree already issued, then further envoys should be sent with strict instructions: wherever conscription is carried out, if the people's hearts show unease, the work must be slowed, with secret memorials for decision, so that later troubles may be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty feels bound by a decree already promulgated, then send further envoys with stern orders: wherever conscription proceeds, if the people show any sign of unrest, slow the levy at once and report secretly for the throne's decision, so that later troubles may be averted.

sentences.zh: 」上嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the memorial and acted on it.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，布衣翟馬周擊登聞鼓，訟昉居宰相位，當北方有事之時，不為邊備，徒知賦詩宴樂。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duan Gong, the commoner Zhai Mazhou struck the petition drum, accusing Fang of holding the chief minister's seat yet, when the north had business, making no frontier preparations and only composing poetry and holding feasts.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Duan Gong era, a commoner named Zhai Mazhou struck the petition drum, charging that while Fang sat as chief minister and the north was in crisis, he made no preparations for the frontier but only wrote poetry and gave banquets.

sentences.zh: 屬耤田禮方畢，乃詔學士賈黃中草制，罷昉為右僕射，且加切責。

translations.literal: When the plowing ceremony had just ended, the emperor ordered Academician Jia Huangzhong to draft an edict, removing Fang to Right Vice Director and adding a stern rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the plowing ceremony had concluded, the emperor ordered Academician Jia Huangzhong to draft an edict demoting Fang to Right Vice Director with a sharp reprimand.

sentences.zh: 黃中言：「僕射，百僚師長，實宰相之任，今自工部尚書而遷是職，非黜責也。

translations.literal: Huangzhong said: "The Vice Director is the head of all officials and in truth holds the chief minister's charge; to move from Minister of Works to this post is not a demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong said, "The Vice Director is the senior of all officials and in substance holds the chief minister's role; promotion from Minister of Works to this office is not a punishment.

sentences.zh: 若曰文昌務簡，以均勞逸為辭，斯為得體。

translations.literal: If it is said that affairs at the Secretariat are to be simplified and labor balanced for rest, that would be proper form.
translations.idiomatic: If the edict speaks of easing duties at the Secretariat and sharing the burden for the sake of repose, that would be fitting.

sentences.zh: 」上然之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 會邊警益急，詔文武群臣各進策備禦，昉又引漢、唐故事，深以屈己修好、弭兵息民為言，時論稱之。

translations.literal: When frontier alarms grew urgent, the emperor ordered civil and military officials each to submit plans for defense; Fang again cited Han and Tang precedents, urging deeply that the throne humble itself to seek good relations, cease arms, and give the people rest; contemporaries praised him.
translations.idiomatic: As frontier alarms intensified, the court ordered civil and military officials to submit plans for defense; Fang again drew on Han and Tang precedents, urging the emperor to humble himself in seeking peace, halt the fighting, and let the people rest—an argument widely praised.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，復以本官兼中書侍郎、平章事，監修國史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua he again held his former office together with Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, supervising compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua he was again made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor while retaining his former rank, with charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 三年夏，旱蝗，既雨。

translations.literal: In the summer of the third year drought and locusts came; afterward rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the third year drought and locusts struck; rain followed.

sentences.zh: 時昉與張齊賢、賈黃中、李沆同居宰輔，以燮理非材，上表待罪，上不之罪。

translations.literal: At the time Fang served in the chief ministry together with Zhang Qixian, Jia Huangzhong, and Li Hang; deeming themselves unfit to harmonize governance, they submitted memorials awaiting punishment, but the emperor did not blame them.
translations.idiomatic: Fang then shared the chief ministry with Zhang Qixian, Jia Huangzhong, and Li Hang; judging themselves unequal to the task of governing, they submitted memorials asking to be punished, but the emperor declined to reproach them.

sentences.zh: 四年，昉以私門連遭憂戚，求解機務，詔不允，遣齊賢等諭旨，復起視事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Fang, his household having suffered repeated bereavements, sought release from state affairs; the edict did not permit it, and Qixian and others were sent to convey the imperial will, after which he resumed office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, with his family struck by repeated mourning, Fang asked to be relieved of high office; the emperor refused, sent Qixian and others to explain his wishes, and Fang returned to duty.

sentences.zh: 後數月，罷為右僕射。

translations.literal: Several months later he was removed to Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later he was demoted to Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 先是，上召張洎草制，授昉左僕射，罷相，洎言：「昉居燮理之任，而陰陽乖戾，不能決意引退，俾居百僚師長之任，何以示勸？

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had summoned Zhang Ji to draft an edict appointing Fang Left Vice Director and removing him from the chief ministry; Ji said: "Fang held the charge of harmonizing governance, yet yin and yang were out of accord and he could not resolve to withdraw; to place him in the seat that heads all officials—how can that serve as encouragement?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had Zhang Ji draft an edict making Fang Left Vice Director and removing him from the chief ministry; Ji argued, "Fang held the task of governing the realm, yet heaven and earth were out of harmony and he would not step down; to set him in the post that heads all officials—what lesson does that teach?

sentences.zh: 」上覽奏，乃令罷守本官。

translations.literal: When the emperor read the memorial, he ordered Fang to resign and keep his original office.
translations.idiomatic: After reading Ji's memorial, the emperor ordered Fang dismissed from the chief ministry but left in his former rank.

sentences.zh: 晉侍中崧者，與昉同宗且同里，時人謂崧為東李家，昉為西李家。

translations.literal: The Jin Vice Director Song was of the same clan and the same village as Fang; people of the time called Song's house the eastern Li family and Fang's the western Li family.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Vice Director Song was Fang's clansman and fellow townsman; contemporaries called Song's branch the eastern Li family and Fang's the western Li family.

sentences.zh: 漢末，崧被誅。

translations.literal: At the end of Han, Song was executed.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Later Han, Song was put to death.

sentences.zh: 至是，其子璨自蘇州常熟縣令赴調，昉為訟其父冤，且言：「周太祖已為昭雪贈官，還其田宅，錄璨而官之。

translations.literal: By this time his son Can came from magistrate of Changshu in Suzhou to await appointment; Fang memorialized on his father's injustice, saying also: "Emperor Taizu of Zhou had already posthumously cleared his name, granted office, and returned his fields and houses, and enrolled Can in office.
translations.idiomatic: Now his son Can arrived from his post as magistrate of Changshu in Suzhou to seek a new appointment; Fang petitioned to redress his father's wrong, adding, "Emperor Taizu of Zhou had already posthumously rehabilitated him, granted him office, restored his lands and house, and given Can an appointment.

sentences.zh: 然璨年幾五十，尚淹州縣之職，臣昔與之同難，豈宜叨遇聖明。

translations.literal: Yet Can is nearly fifty and still lingers in prefectural posts; your servant once shared his family's calamity—how can he presume on holy clarity?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Can is nearly fifty and still stuck in county and prefectural posts; I once shared his family's ruin—how should he presume on Your Majesty's grace?

sentences.zh: 儻推一視之仁，澤及衰微之祚，則已往之冤獲伸於下，而繼絕之恩永光簡冊矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty extends the kindness of treating all alike and its grace reaches a declining line, then past wrongs will be vindicated below and the grace of continuing a severed line will forever shine in the annals.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty extends equal mercy to the fallen and favors a house in decline, then old wrongs will be righted in this life and the grace of continuing a cut-off line will shine forever in the records.

sentences.zh: 」詔授璨著作佐郎，後官至右讚善大夫。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Can Assistant Compiler; he later reached Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The throne appointed Can Assistant Compiler; he later rose to Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二年，陪祀南郊，禮畢入賀，因拜舞仆地，臺吏掖之以出，臥疾數日薨，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the second year, accompanying the sacrifice at the Southern Suburb, when the rites ended he entered to offer congratulations, then bowed and fell prostrate; clerks of the Censorate helped him out; after several days of illness he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, while attending the suburban sacrifice, he entered to offer congratulations after the rites, bowed, and collapsed; censorate clerks helped him out; he lay ill for several days and died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒，諡文正。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Mentor and given the posthumous title Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Mentor with the temple name Wenzheng.

sentences.zh: 昉和厚多恕，不念舊惡，在位小心循謹，無赫赫稱。

translations.literal: Fang was mild and thick, greatly forgiving, and did not bear old grudges; in office he was careful and deferential, without striking renown.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was gentle and magnanimous, slow to remember injuries; in office he was cautious and meticulous, without showy reputation.

sentences.zh: 為文章慕白居易，尤淺近易曉。

translations.literal: In writing he admired Bai Juyi, especially shallow and easy to understand.
translations.idiomatic: As a writer he took Bai Juyi as his model, favoring language plain and readily understood.

sentences.zh: 好接賓客，江南平，士大夫歸朝者多從之遊。

translations.literal: He loved receiving guests; after the south was pacified, many scholars returning to court associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in entertaining guests; after the conquest of the south, many southern scholars newly arrived at court sought his company.

sentences.zh: 雅厚張洎而薄張佖，及昉罷相，洎草制深攻詆之，而佖朔望必詣昉。

translations.literal: He favored Zhang Ji deeply and looked coldly on Zhang Yi; when Fang left the chief ministry, Ji drafted the edict and attacked him harshly, yet Yi on the first and fifteenth of each month always called on Fang.
translations.idiomatic: He held Zhang Ji in high regard but thought little of Zhang Yi; when Fang left office, Ji drafted the edict and vilified him bitterly, yet Yi still visited Fang on every first and fifteenth of the month.

sentences.zh: 或謂佖曰：「李公待君素不厚，何數詣之？

translations.literal: Someone asked Yi: "Lord Li has never treated you warmly—why do you visit so often?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Yi, "Lord Li has never favored you—why do you call on him so often?

sentences.zh: 」佖曰：「我為廷尉日，李公方秉政，未嘗一有請求，此吾所以重之也。」

translations.literal: Yi said: "In my days as Commandant of Justice, when Lord Li held power, he never once made a request of me—that is why I respect him."
translations.idiomatic: Yi replied, "When I was Commandant of Justice and Lord Li was in power, he never once asked a favor of me—that is why I hold him in esteem."

sentences.zh: 昉所居有園亭別墅之勝，多召故人親友宴樂其中。

translations.literal: Fang's residence had the beauty of gardens, pavilions, and villas; he often summoned old friends and kin to feast and make merry there.
translations.idiomatic: His home boasted gardens, pavilions, and country villas; he often gathered old friends and relatives there for feasting and pleasure.

sentences.zh: 既致政，欲尋洛中九老故事，時吏部尚書宋琪年七十九，左諫議大夫楊徽之年七十五，郢州刺史魏丕年七十六，太常少卿致仕李運年八十，水部郎中朱昂年七十一，廬州節度副使武允成年七十九，太子中允致仕張好問年八十五，吳僧讚寧年七十八，議將集，會蜀寇而罷。

translations.literal: After he retired from office he wished to revive the story of the Nine Old Men of Luoyang: at the time Minister of Personnel Song Qi was seventy-nine, Left Remonstrator Yang Weizhi seventy-five, Prefect of Ying Wei Pi seventy-six, Retired Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Li Yun eighty, Director in the Ministry of Water Zhu Ang seventy-one, Military Vice Commissioner of Luzhou Wu Yongnian seventy-nine, Retired Crown Prince's Attendant Zhang Haowen eighty-five, the Wu monk Zanning seventy-eight—they planned to assemble, but bandits in Shu caused it to be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: After retirement he hoped to revive the tradition of the Nine Old Men of Luoyang: Minister of Personnel Song Qi was seventy-nine, Left Remonstrator Yang Weizhi seventy-five, Prefect of Ying Wei Pi seventy-six, retired Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Li Yun eighty, Director in the Ministry of Water Zhu Ang seventy-one, Military Vice Commissioner of Luzhou Wu Yongnian seventy-nine, retired Crown Prince's Attendant Zhang Haowen eighty-five, and the Wu monk Zanning seventy-eight—they meant to gather, but unrest in Shu forced them to abandon the plan.

sentences.zh: 昉素與盧多遜善，待之不疑，多遜屢譖昉於上，或以告昉，不之信。

translations.literal: Fang had long been on good terms with Lu Duosun and trusted him without doubt; Duosun several times slandered Fang to the emperor, and when some told Fang, he did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had long been close to Lu Duosun and trusted him without reserve; Duosun repeatedly slandered Fang to the throne, and though others warned him, Fang refused to believe it.

sentences.zh: 及入相，太宗言及多遜事，昉頗為解釋。

translations.literal: When he entered the chief ministry, Emperor Taizong spoke of Duosun's conduct, and Fang offered considerable explanation in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: After he became chief minister, Emperor Taizong spoke of Duosun's actions, and Fang offered a spirited defense.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「多遜居常毀卿一錢不直。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Duosun in ordinary times says you are not worth a single cash.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Duosun routinely says you are not worth a single coin.

sentences.zh: 」昉始信之。

translations.literal: Only then did Fang believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Fang believe the reports.

sentences.zh: 上由此益重昉。

translations.literal: Because of this the emperor esteemed Fang all the more.
translations.idiomatic: From this the emperor valued Fang still more highly.

sentences.zh: 昉居中書日，有求進用者，雖知其材可取，必正色拒絕之，已而擢用；

translations.literal: When Fang was in the Secretariat, if someone sought advancement, though he knew the man's talent was acceptable he would sternly refuse; afterward he would promote him.
translations.idiomatic: While Fang sat in the Secretariat, those who sought promotion—even when he knew their talent merited use—were met with a stern refusal; yet afterward he would advance them.

sentences.zh: 或不足用，必和顏溫語待之。

translations.literal: If someone was not fit for use, he would receive him with a gentle face and warm words.
translations.idiomatic: Those unfit for appointment he received with a kindly manner and gentle speech.

sentences.zh: 子弟問其故，曰：「用賢，人主之事；

translations.literal: His sons and younger relatives asked the reason; he said: "Employing the worthy is the ruler's affair.
translations.idiomatic: When his sons and nephews asked why, he said, "Putting the worthy in office is the ruler's business.

sentences.zh: 若受其請，是市私恩也，故峻絕之，使恩歸於上。

translations.literal: If one accepts their request, that is trading private favor; therefore I refuse them sternly so that the grace returns to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: To accept their pleas is to trade in private favor; so I refuse them harshly and let the credit belong to the throne.

sentences.zh: 若不用者，既失所望，又無善辭，取怨之道也。」

translations.literal: If they are not used, having lost what they hoped for and having no kind words, that is the way to incur resentment."
translations.idiomatic: If they are not appointed, they have lost their hope and receive no gracious reply—that is how resentment is bred."

sentences.zh: 初，超未有子，昉母謝方娠，指腹謂伯母張曰：「生男當與伯母為子。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chao had no son yet, Fang's mother Xie was pregnant; pointing at her belly she told her sister-in-law Zhang: "If a boy is born, he shall be son to my sister-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, before Chao had a son, Fang's mother Xie was pregnant; she pointed at her belly and told her sister-in-law Zhang, "If I bear a son, he shall be your son.

sentences.zh: 」故昉出繼於超。

translations.literal: Therefore Fang was given in adoption to Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Fang was adopted as Chao's heir.

sentences.zh: 昉再相，因表其事，求贈所生父母官。

translations.literal: When Fang became chief minister a second time, he memorialized on the matter and asked posthumous offices for his birth parents.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang served as chief minister again, he submitted a memorial on the matter and asked that offices be granted his biological parents.

sentences.zh: 詔贈其祖溫太子太傅，祖母權氏莒國太夫人，起太子太師，謝氏鄭國太夫人。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made his grandfather Wen Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, his grandmother Lady Quan Lady of Ju, Qi Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Lady Xie Lady of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: The throne posthumously honored his grandfather Wen as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, his grandmother Lady Quan as Lady of the State of Ju, his father Qi as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and his mother Lady Xie as Lady of the State of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 昉素病心悸，數歲一發，發必彌年而後愈，蓋典誥命三十餘年，勞役思慮所致。

translations.literal: Fang had long suffered palpitations of the heart; every few years it would flare, and when it flared it would last nearly a year before recovery—probably from drafting edicts for more than thirty years and the labor of thought.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had long suffered heart palpitations; every few years they recurred, and each attack lasted nearly a year before he recovered—likely the toll of drafting edicts for more than thirty years.

sentences.zh: 及居相位，益加憂畏。

translations.literal: When he reached the chief ministry, his worry and fear increased.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held the chief ministry, his anxiety only grew.

sentences.zh: 有文集五十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in fifty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to fifty juan.

sentences.zh: 子四人：宗訥、宗誨、宗諤、宗諒。

translations.literal: He had four sons: Zongne, Zonghui, Zong'e, and Zongliang.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Zongne, Zonghui, Zong'e, and Zongliang.

sentences.zh: 宗誨，右讚善大夫。

translations.literal: Zonghui was Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghui served as Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 宗諒，主賓客員外郎。

translations.literal: Zongliang was Vice Director of the Bureau of Receptions.
translations.idiomatic: Zongliang was Vice Director of the Bureau of Receptions.

sentences.zh: 子 宗訥

translations.literal: Son Zongne
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongne

sentences.zh: 宗訥，字大辨，以蔭補太廟齋郎，遷第四室長。

translations.literal: Zongne, style name Dabian, through yin privilege was made Aide of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and was transferred to chief of the fourth shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Zongne, styled Dabian, entered service through yin privilege as Aide of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and was promoted to chief of the fourth shrine.

sentences.zh: 代謁吏部銓，邊光範意其年少，未能屬辭，語之曰：「苟援筆成六韻詩，雖不試書判，可入等矣。

translations.literal: Replacing his father at the Ministry of Personnel selection, Bian Guangfan thought him young and unable to compose documents, and said to him: "If you can take up the brush and complete a regulated poem in six rhymes, though you are not tested in document judgment, you may enter the grade.
translations.idiomatic: When he stood in for his father at the Ministry's selection board, Bian Guangfan thought him too young to draft documents and said, "If you can write a regulated verse in six rhymes on the spot, you may pass the grade even without the document test.

sentences.zh: 」宗訥易之，光範試詩賦，立就。

translations.literal: Zongne agreed; Guangfan tested him in poetry and fu, and he finished at once.
translations.idiomatic: Zongne agreed; Guangfan tested him in poetry and fu, and he completed them immediately.

sentences.zh: 明日，遂擬授秘書省正字；

translations.literal: The next day he was provisionally appointed Proofreader of the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was provisionally named Proofreader of the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 又明日，上命擢國子監丞。

translations.literal: the day after, the emperor ordered him promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: the day after that the emperor ordered him promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 蓋上居藩邸時，每有篇詠，令昉屬和，前後數百章，皆宗訥繕寫，上愛其楷麗，問知為宗訥所書，故有是命。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was in the princely residence, whenever he had a poem he ordered Fang to harmonize with it; several hundred pieces before and after were all copied by Zongne; the emperor loved their regular beauty, asked who had written them, learned it was Zongne, and therefore gave this order.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor still lived in the princely residence, each time he composed a poem he had Fang write a matching verse; several hundred such pieces were all transcribed by Zongne; the emperor admired the elegant regular script, learned Zongne had written them, and therefore issued this command.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，詔賈黃中集《神醫普救方》，宗訥暨劉錫、吳淑、呂文仲、杜鎬、舒雅皆預焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo an edict ordered Jia Huangzhong to compile the Comprehensive Relief Formulas of the Divine Physician; Zongne together with Liu Xi, Wu Shu, Lü Wenzhong, Du Hao, and Shu Ya all took part.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Taiping Xingguo the court ordered Jia Huangzhong to compile the Comprehensive Relief Formulas of the Divine Physician; Zongne joined Liu Xi, Wu Shu, Lü Wenzhong, Du Hao, and Shu Ya in the work.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，昉在相位，上欲命宗訥為尚書郎，昉懇辭，以為非承平故事，止改秘書丞，歷太常博士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi, when Fang was chief minister, the emperor wished to appoint Zongne Secretariat Director; Fang earnestly declined, holding that it was not precedent in peaceful times, and he stopped at Secretariat Vice Director, passing through Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongxi, while Fang was chief minister, the emperor wished to make Zongne a Secretariat Director; Fang firmly declined, arguing it was not custom in settled times, and Zongne remained Secretariat Vice Director, later serving as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 宗訥頗習典禮。

translations.literal: Zongne was quite versed in ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Zongne was well versed in ritual protocol.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，呂端掌禮院，引宗訥同判，累遷比部郎中。

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era Lü Duan directed the Ritual Institute and brought Zongne in as joint judge; he was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: During Chunhua, Lü Duan headed the Ritual Institute and brought Zongne in as associate director; Zongne rose step by step to Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 咸平六年，卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianping he died, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xianping he died at fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 子昭迴，大中祥符五年獻文，召試賜進士第，後為屯田員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Zhaohui, in the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, presented a literary work, was summoned for examination and granted jinshi, and later became Vice Director of the Bureau of State Farms.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhaohui, in the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, submitted a literary work, was examined at court and given the jinshi degree, and later served as Vice Director of the Bureau of State Farms.

sentences.zh: 昭遜，太子中舍。

translations.literal: Zhaoxun was Attendant of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoxun was Attendant of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 子 宗諤

translations.literal: Son Zong'e
translations.idiomatic: His son Zong'e

sentences.zh: 宗諤，字昌武，七歲能屬文，恥以父蔭得官，獨由鄉舉，第進士，授校書郎。

translations.literal: Zong'e, style name Changwu, at seven could compose prose, was ashamed to gain office through his father's yin privilege, and entered solely by provincial examination, placing as jinshi, appointed Proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: Zong'e, styled Changwu, could write prose at seven; ashamed to take office through his father's privilege, he entered service only by the provincial examinations, passed as jinshi, and was made Proofreader.

sentences.zh: 明年，獻文自薦，遷秘書郎、集賢校理、同修起居注。

translations.literal: The next year he presented a literary work recommending himself and was moved to Secretariat Gentleman, Collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and Compiler of the Diary of Activity and Repose.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he submitted a self-recommended literary work and was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman, Collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and Compiler of the Diary of Activity and Repose.

sentences.zh: 先是，後苑陪宴，校理官不與，京官乘馬不得入禁門。

translations.literal: Earlier, at banquets in the rear park, collators did not attend, and capital officials riding horses could not enter the forbidden gate.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, at banquets in the rear park, collators were not invited, and capital officials on horseback were barred from the inner gate.

sentences.zh: 至是，皆因宗諤之請復之，遂為故事。

translations.literal: By this time both were restored at Zong'e's request and thereafter became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Now both privileges were restored at Zong'e's petition and thereafter became fixed practice.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，拜起居舍人，預重修《太祖實錄》。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong took the throne, he was made Drafter of Activity and Repose and took part in the comprehensive revision of the Veritable Records of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong ascended the throne, Zong'e was made Drafter of Activity and Repose and helped revise the Veritable Records of Taizu.

sentences.zh: 從幸大名，上疏曰：「國家馭邊之術，制勝之謀，將帥之短長，兵衛之眾寡，宸算廟謨，盡在吾術中矣。

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor to Daming, he submitted a memorial saying: "The state's methods for controlling the frontier, plans for victory, generals' strengths and weaknesses, and the numbers of the guard—the imperial calculations and temple strategies are all in our manuals.
translations.idiomatic: On the journey to Daming he submitted a memorial: "The state's frontier policy, its plans for victory, the strengths and weaknesses of its commanders, and the size of the guard—the court's calculations and secret strategies are all set down in our books.

sentences.zh: 今之言事者，不過請陛下益兵貯糧，分道掩殺，言之甚易，行之則難。

translations.literal: Those who speak on affairs today only ask Your Majesty to increase troops and store grain, divide forces for ambush and slaughter—easy to say, hard to do.
translations.idiomatic: Today's advisers do nothing but urge Your Majesty to raise more troops, stock more grain, and send columns to raid and kill—the words are easy; the deeds are hard.

sentences.zh: 始受命則無不以攻堅陷陣為壯圖，及遇敵則惟以閉壘塞關為上計，孤君父之重委，致生靈之重困，興言及此，誠可歎息。

translations.literal: At first receiving orders none fail to picture storming strongholds as a bold design, yet on meeting the enemy they take closing passes and blocking gates as the highest plan, betraying the ruler-father's weighty trust and bringing the people's heavy distress—to speak of this is truly lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: At first every commander vows to storm walls and break lines; yet when the enemy appears the highest wisdom is to shut the passes and bar the gates, betraying the heavy trust of ruler and father and plunging the people into misery—at the thought one can only sigh.

sentences.zh: 自古行軍出師，無不首擇將帥。

translations.literal: Since antiquity in marching armies and expeditions, none has failed first to choose generals.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity no army has marched without first choosing its commanders.

sentences.zh: 夫將帥隨材任使，守一郡，控一城，分領驍勇，爭據要害，又豈直三路主帥之名，然後能制六師生死之命乎？

translations.literal: Generals are assigned according to talent, guarding one commandery, holding one walled city, dividing command of the brave, contesting key points—must they bear only the title of commander of the three routes before they can control the life and death of the Six Armies?
translations.idiomatic: Commanders should be matched to their gifts—holding one district, defending one walled city, leading the bold to seize vital ground—need they bear only the title of commander of the three routes before they can hold the fate of the Six Armies in their hands?

sentences.zh: 今陛下選任非不至也，權位非不重也，告戒非不丁寧也，處置非不專一也；

translations.literal: Today Your Majesty's selection is not insufficient, authority not light, admonitions not lacking in earnestness, disposition not lacking in concentration;
translations.idiomatic: Today Your Majesty's appointments are not wanting, their powers not slight, your warnings not lacking in earnestness, your orders not lacking in focus;

sentences.zh: 而外敵犯塞，車駕親征，曾不聞出一人一騎為之救助，不知深溝高壘，秣馬厲兵，欲安用哉？

translations.literal: yet when outer enemies violate the passes and the imperial carriage campaigns in person, one never hears of a single man or horse sent to their aid—one does not know deep moats, high ramparts, fat horses, and sharpened weapons—of what use are they?
translations.idiomatic: yet when enemies cross the border and the emperor campaigns in person, not a single rider is sent to their relief; if deep moats, high walls, fed horses, and honed blades serve no purpose, what are they for?

sentences.zh: 臣以為臨軍易帥，拔卒為將，在此時也。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that changing commanders on the eve of battle and plucking soldiers to make generals is for this moment.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that replacing commanders on the eve of battle and promoting soldiers to generalship is what the moment demands.

sentences.zh: 有功者拔於朝，不用者戮於市，亦此時也。

translations.literal: Those with merit to be pulled up at court, those not used to be executed in the market—that too is for this moment.
translations.idiomatic: Reward the successful at court; execute the useless in the marketplace—that too is for this moment.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下圖之。

translations.literal: Only Your Majesty should plan it.
translations.idiomatic: Only Your Majesty can decide.

sentences.zh: 然後下哀痛之詔，行蠲復之恩。

translations.literal: Then issue the edict of deep grief and enact the grace of tax relief.
translations.idiomatic: Then issue an edict of compassion and grant tax remissions.

sentences.zh: 回鸞上都，垂衣當寧，豈不盛哉。」

translations.literal: Turn the imperial carriage to the capital, let robes hang in ease at the throne—would that not be glorious?"
translations.idiomatic: Return the imperial procession to the capital and rule at ease from the throne—would that not be magnificent?"

sentences.zh: 遷知制誥、判集賢院，纂《西垣集制》，刻石記名氏。

translations.literal: He was moved to Drafting Secretary and given charge of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, compiling the Western Wall Collected Drafts and carving stone to record names.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Drafting Secretary and put in charge of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, compiling the Western Wall Collected Drafts and having names cut in stone.

sentences.zh: 嘗牒御史臺不平空，中丞呂文仲移文詰之，往復再三。

translations.literal: Once he petitioned the Censorate that its quarters were cramped; Vice Censor Lü Wenzhong sent documents questioning him, and they exchanged several rounds.
translations.idiomatic: Once he petitioned the Censorate that its offices were too cramped; Vice Censor Lü Wenzhong sent formal queries, and they exchanged several rounds of argument.

sentences.zh: 宗諤執言兩省故事與臺司不相統攝者凡八。

translations.literal: Zong'e held that between the two inner departments and the Censorate there were eight precedents of non-supervision in all.
translations.idiomatic: Zong'e cited eight precedents by which the two inner departments and the Censorate did not supervise one another.

sentences.zh: 事聞，卒如宗諤議。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, in the end it followed Zong'e's view.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter reached the throne, the court ruled as Zong'e had argued.

sentences.zh: 景德二年，召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingde he was summoned as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingde he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 是秋，將郊，命判太常大樂、鼓吹二署。

translations.literal: That autumn, when the suburban sacrifice was near, he was ordered to direct the Great Music Office and the Office of Drum and Pipe Music.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, as the suburban sacrifice approached, he was ordered to oversee the Great Music Office and the Office of Drum and Pipe Music.

sentences.zh: 先是，樂工率以年勞遷補，至有抱其器而不知聲者。

translations.literal: Earlier, musicians were generally promoted through seniority by years of service, until some embraced their instruments yet did not know sound.
translations.idiomatic: Previously musicians were promoted chiefly by seniority, until some clutched their instruments yet knew nothing of music.

sentences.zh: 宗諤素曉音律，遂加審定，奏斥謬濫者五十人。

translations.literal: Zong'e had long understood pitch and regulation; he therefore added scrutiny and memorialized to dismiss fifty who were false or excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Zong'e had long understood pitch and mode; he added scrutiny and memorialized to dismiss fifty unqualified performers.

sentences.zh: 因修完器具，更署職名，條上利病二十事，帝省閱而賞歎之。

translations.literal: He then repaired and completed instruments, renewed office titles, and listed twenty items of benefit and harm; the emperor reviewed them and praised them.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the instruments, revised office titles, and submitted twenty recommendations for reform; the emperor read them and expressed his admiration.

sentences.zh: 事具《樂志》。

translations.literal: The matter is fully set forth in the Treatise on Music.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the Treatise on Music.

sentences.zh: 又著《樂纂》以獻，命付史館，自是月再肄習焉。

translations.literal: He also composed a Music Compendium and presented it; he was ordered to deposit it in the Historiography Institute, and thereafter practice was held twice a month.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote a Music Compendium and presented it; the court ordered it filed in the Historiography Institute, and thereafter rehearsals were held twice monthly.

sentences.zh: 時諸神祠壇多闕外壝之制，因深塹列樹以表之，營葺齋室，舊典因以振起。

translations.literal: At the time many spirit shrines lacked outer enclosure regulations; he therefore dug deep ditches and planted rows of trees to mark them, built and repaired fasting halls, and old rites were thereby revived.
translations.idiomatic: Many spirit altars then lacked proper outer enclosures; he dug deep trenches and planted rows of trees to mark them, rebuilt the fasting halls, and ancient rites were thereby restored.

sentences.zh: 屬契丹遣使來賀承天節，詔宗諤為館伴使，自郊勞至飲餞，皆刊定其儀。

translations.literal: When the Khitan sent envoys to congratulate the Chengtian Festival, an edict made Zong'e hosting commissioner; from suburban greeting to the farewell feast he edited and fixed all the ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan sent envoys for the Chengtian Festival, Zong'e was named hosting commissioner; from the suburban welcome to the farewell banquet he revised every ceremony.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，從封泰山，改工部郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu, accompanying the feng and shan rites at Mount Tai, he was changed to Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dazhong Xiangfu, on the feng and shan journey to Mount Tai, he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 二年，始建昭應宮，命副丁謂為同修宮使。

translations.literal: In the second year, when the Zhaoying Palace was first built, he was ordered assistant to Ding Wei as Commissioner for Joint Construction of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when construction of the Zhaoying Palace began, he was made Ding Wei's deputy as Commissioner for Joint Construction.

sentences.zh: 三年，知審官院。

translations.literal: In the third year he was given charge of the Bureau for Review of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was put in charge of the Bureau for Review of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 屬祀汾陰后土，命為經度制置副使，同權河中府事。

translations.literal: When sacrifices were made at Fenyin to the Queen of Earth, he was made Vice Commissioner for Planning and Arrangement and jointly given temporary authority over the Hezhong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For the Fenyin sacrifice to the Queen of Earth he was named Vice Commissioner for Planning and Arrangement and given joint temporary authority over Hezhong prefecture.

sentences.zh: 禮成，優拜右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed he was graciously promoted to Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: After the rites he was graciously promoted to Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍宴玉宸殿，上謂曰：「聞卿至孝，宗族頗多，長幼雍睦。

translations.literal: Once attending a feast in the Hall of Jade Purity, the emperor said to him: "I hear you are deeply filial and your clan is numerous, elders and juniors harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet in the Hall of Jade Purity the emperor told him, "I hear you are deeply filial, your clan numerous, and elders and juniors live in harmony.

sentences.zh: 朕嗣守二聖基業，亦如卿之保守門戶也。

translations.literal: I inherit and guard the foundations of the two sage emperors, just as you guard your household gate.
translations.idiomatic: I inherit and guard the foundations laid by the two sage emperors, much as you guard your family's gate.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「翰林，清華之地，前賢敭曆，多有故事，卿父子為之，必周知也。

translations.literal: He also said: "The Hanlin is a pure and splendid place; former worthies who rose through it left many stories—you father and son in it must know them thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "The Hanlin is a pure and eminent office; the worthies who passed through it left many precedents—you and your father in that hall must know them well.

sentences.zh: 」宗諤嘗著《翰林雜記》以紀國朝制度，明日上之。

translations.literal: Zong'e had composed Miscellaneous Records of the Hanlin to record the dynasty's institutions; the next day he presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Zong'e had written Miscellaneous Records of the Hanlin to document the dynasty's institutions; he presented it the next day.

sentences.zh: 宗諤究心典禮，凡創制損益，靡不與聞。

translations.literal: Zong'e devoted his heart to ritual regulations; every new creation, reduction, or increase, there was none he did not hear of.
translations.idiomatic: Zong'e devoted himself to ritual law; every new institution, cutback, or addition passed through his counsel.

sentences.zh: 修定皇親故事、武舉武選入官資敘、閣門儀制、臣僚導從、貢院條貫，餘多裁正。

translations.literal: He revised the regulations for imperial clansmen, the qualifications for military examination candidates entering office, gate protocols, ministers' processions, and examination-yard rules; the rest he mostly corrected.
translations.idiomatic: He revised regulations for imperial clansmen, qualifications for military-examination appointees, gate ceremony, ministers' processions, and examination rules, among much else he set right.

sentences.zh: 五年，迎真州聖像，副丁謂為迎奉使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, welcoming the sacred image at Zhenzhou, he was deputy to Ding Wei as Reception Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when the sacred image was welcomed at Zhenzhou, he served as Ding Wei's deputy Reception Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五月，以疾卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he died of illness, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he died of illness at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 帝甚悼之，謂宰相曰：「國朝將相家，能以聲名自立，不墜門閥，唯昉與曹彬家爾。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply mourned him and told the chief minister: "Among minister-general families of our dynasty, only the houses of Fang and Cao Bin have been able to stand on reputation themselves without the gate falling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved deeply and told the chief minister, "Among our dynasty's great houses, only the families of Fang and Cao Bin have upheld their names without their gates declining.

sentences.zh: 宗諤方期大用，不幸短命，深可惜也。

translations.literal: Zong'e was just at the point of great employment when, unhappily, his life was short—deeply to be regretted.
translations.idiomatic: Zong'e was on the verge of high appointment when his early death cut him off—a loss the court deeply regretted.

sentences.zh: 」既厚賻其家，以白金賜其繼母，又錄其子若弟以官焉。

translations.literal: After richly compensating his family, with white gold he rewarded his stepmother, and also enrolled his sons and younger brothers in office.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave his family a rich burial grant, rewarded his stepmother with white gold, and granted offices to his sons and younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 初，昉居三館、兩制之職，宗諤不數年，皆踐其地。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Fang held posts in the Three Institutes and the two drafting offices, Zong'e within a few years had trodden all those places.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had held every post in the Three Institutes and the two drafting offices; Zong'e within a few years had filled them all.

sentences.zh: 風流儒雅，藏書萬卷。

translations.literal: Refined and elegant in manner, he had ten thousand juan of books in his collection.
translations.idiomatic: Elegant in bearing, he kept a library of ten thousand juan.

sentences.zh: 內行淳至，事繼母符氏以孝聞。

translations.literal: In private conduct he was pure and sincere; in serving his stepmother Lady Fu he was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: In private life he was utterly sincere; his devotion to his stepmother Lady Fu won renown for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 二兄早世，奉嫂字孤，恩禮兼盡。

translations.literal: His two elder brothers died young; he supported his sister-in-law and raised the orphans, kindness and ritual both fully fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Both his elder brothers died young; he cared for his sister-in-law and raised her orphaned children, showing every measure of kindness and propriety.

sentences.zh: 與弟宗諒友愛尤至，覃恩所及，必先群從，及歿而己子有未仕者。

translations.literal: With younger brother Zongliang affection was especially deep; grace extended by the throne, he always put collaterals first; when he died his own sons had some not yet in office.
translations.idiomatic: His bond with his younger brother Zongliang was especially close; whenever imperial favor reached the clan, he always gave his collaterals priority first, and at his death some of his own sons had still not received appointments.

sentences.zh: 程宿早卒，有弟無所依，宗諤為表請於朝而官之。

translations.literal: Cheng Su died young; he had a younger brother with nowhere to rely; Zong'e memorialized the court on his behalf and had him given office.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Su died young, leaving a younger brother with no one to depend on; Zong'e submitted a memorial to the court and secured an appointment for him.

sentences.zh: 勤接士類，無賢不肖，恂恂盡禮，獎拔後進，唯恐不及，以是士人皆歸仰之。

translations.literal: He diligently received scholars, whether worthy or not, respectfully fulfilling ritual; he encouraged and promoted juniors, fearing he might not reach enough—therefore scholars all turned to admire him.
translations.idiomatic: He welcomed scholars tirelessly, treating the worthy and unworthy alike with steady courtesy, promoting younger men whenever he could and fearing he had not done enough; for this scholars everywhere looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 宗諤工隸書。

translations.literal: Zong'e was skilled at clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Zong'e excelled at clerical script.

sentences.zh: 有文集六十卷，《內外制》三十卷。

translations.literal: He had collected works of sixty juan and Inner and Outer Drafts of thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in sixty juan and Inner and Outer Drafts in thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 嘗預修《續通典》、《大中祥符封禪汾陰記》、《諸路圖經》，又作《家傳》、《談錄》，並行於世。

translations.literal: He once took part in compiling the Continued Tongdian, the Dazhong xiangfu Record of the Feng and Fen sacrifices, and provincial route gazetteers; he also wrote Family Traditions and Collected Conversations, all circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He helped compile the Continued Tongdian, the Record of the Dazhong xiangfu Feng and Fen sacrifices, and route gazetteers for the provinces, and also wrote Family Traditions and Collected Conversations, all of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子昭遹、昭述、昭適。

translations.literal: His sons were Zhaoyao, Zhaoshu, and Zhaoshi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Zhaoyao, Zhaoshu, and Zhaoshi.

sentences.zh: 孫 昭述

translations.literal: Grandson: Zhaoshu
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Zhaoshu

sentences.zh: 昭述，字仲祖，以父蔭為秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: Zhaoshu, styled Zhongzu, through his father's privilege became Secretariat proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoshu, styled Zhongzu, entered office through his father's privilege as a proofreader in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 召試學士院，賜進士出身，為刑部詳覆官，累遷秘書丞。

translations.literal: Summoned to examination at the Academy, granted jinshi status, made Ministry of Justice detailed review officer, and repeatedly promoted to Secretariat aide.
translations.idiomatic: Called to examination at the Hanlin Academy, he was granted jinshi standing, served as a detailed-review officer in the Ministry of Justice, and rose to Secretariat aide.

sentences.zh: 群牧制置使曹利用薦為判官，鄆州牧地侵於民者凡數千頃，昭述悉復之。

translations.literal: Commissioner for Herds Cao Liyong recommended him as administrative aide; in Yanzhou pasture lands encroaching on the people totaled several thousand qing—Zhaoshu fully restored them all.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Liyong, commissioner for herds, recommended him as an administrative aide; in Yanzhou thousands of qing of pastureland had been taken from commoners, and Zhaoshu restored all of it.

sentences.zh: 以太常博士知開封縣，特遷尚書屯田員外郎、開封推官。

translations.literal: As Erudite of the Grand Secretariat he governed Kaifeng County, specially promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue's Farms Bureau and Kaifeng investigating commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: As an erudite of the Grand Secretariat he governed Kaifeng County, then was specially promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue's farms bureau and investigating commissioner for Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 坐嘗被曹利用薦，出知常州，遷為三司度支判官，改河北轉運使。

translations.literal: Because he had once been recommended by Cao Liyong, he was sent out to govern Changzhou, then moved to be Three Departments fiscal administrative aide, and changed to Hebei transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had once been recommended by Cao Liyong, he was posted out to govern Changzhou, then became a fiscal administrative aide in the Three Departments and was transferred to Hebei transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 江陵屯兵讙言倉粟陳腐，欲以動眾。

translations.literal: At Jiangling the garrison troops clamored that the granary grain was stale and rotten, intending to stir up the masses.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangling the garrison troops spread word that the granary grain was stale and rotten, hoping to stir up a mutiny.

sentences.zh: 昭述取以為奉，且以飯其僚屬，眾遂定。

translations.literal: Zhaoshu took it for his own provisions and also used it to feed his subordinates; the crowd then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoshu took the grain for his own table and fed his staff from it as well, and the troops quieted down.

sentences.zh: 徙湖南潭州，戍卒憤監軍酷暴，欲構亂，或指昭述謂曰：「如李公長者，何可負？

translations.literal: Transferred to Tanzhou in Hunan; garrison troops, enraged at the supervising commander's cruelty and violence, wished to plot rebellion. Someone pointed at Zhaoshu and said: "As for Lord Li, a man of worth—how could we betray him?
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Tanzhou in Hunan, the garrison troops, furious at their supervising commander's cruelty, plotted mutiny; someone pointed to Zhaoshu and said, "A man like Lord Li—a true elder—how could we turn against him?

sentences.zh: 」其謀遂寢。

translations.literal: " Their plot then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: " With that the plot collapsed.

sentences.zh: 昭述聞之，以戒監軍。

translations.literal: When Zhaoshu heard of it, he used it to admonish the supervising commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaoshu heard of this, he used it to warn the supervising commander.

sentences.zh: 監軍自是不復為暴。

translations.literal: The supervising commander from then on no longer acted with violence.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising commander never again abused his authority.

sentences.zh: 比去，眾遮道羅拜，指妻子曰：「嚮非公，無噍類矣。」

translations.literal: When he was about to leave, the crowd blocked the road and bowed in rows, pointing to their wives and children and saying: "Had it not been for you, sir, we would have had no one left to eat."
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to depart, people blocked the road and bowed in rows, pointing to their wives and children and saying, "If not for you, sir, none of us would be alive."

sentences.zh: 徙淮南轉運使兼發運使，加直史館。

translations.literal: Transferred to Huainan transport commissioner and concurrently grain dispatch commissioner, added as Drafter of the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Huainan transport commissioner and concurrently grain dispatch commissioner, and was made a drafter of the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 徙陝西轉運使，糾察在京刑獄，為三司戶部副使，累遷刑部郎中。

translations.literal: Transferred to Shaanxi transport commissioner, inspected capital criminal prisons, made Three Departments vice commissioner of the Household Bureau, and repeatedly promoted to Ministry of Justice director.
translations.idiomatic: He became Shaanxi transport commissioner, inspected criminal cases in the capital, served as a Three Departments vice commissioner of the household bureau, and rose to director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 陝西用兵，提點陝西計置糧草，還授度支、鹽鐵副使，以右諫議大夫為河北都轉運使。

translations.literal: When Shaanxi was at war, he supervised Shaanxi planning and provisioning of grain and fodder; on return he was given fiscal and salt-and-iron vice commissioner posts, and as Right Remonstrance Grand Master became overall Hebei transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaanxi campaign he oversaw grain and fodder for the frontier; on his return he was made fiscal and salt-and-iron vice commissioner, and as right remonstrance grand master he became overall Hebei transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 河決澶淵，久未塞。

translations.literal: The Yellow River burst its banks at Chanyuan and for a long time was not closed.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River had breached its banks at Chanyuan and long remained unstopped.

sentences.zh: 會契丹遣劉六符來，乃命昭述城澶州，以治堤為名，調兵農八萬，逾旬而就。

translations.literal: When the Khitan sent Liu Liufu on a mission, he was ordered to fortify Chanyuan—under the name of repairing the dike—and mobilized eighty thousand soldiers and farmers; in little more than ten days it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan sent Liu Liufu on a mission, the court ordered Zhaoshu to fortify Chanyuan under the pretext of repairing the dike; he mobilized eighty thousand soldiers and farmers, and the work was finished in little more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 初，六符過之，真以為堤也，及還而城具，甚駭愕。

translations.literal: At first when Liufu passed by, he truly thought it was a dike; when he returned the city was complete, and he was greatly startled.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Liufu first passed through, he took it for a dike repair; on his return the fortress stood complete, and he was deeply astonished.

sentences.zh: 初置義勇軍，人情洶洶，昭述乘疾置日行數舍，開諭父老，眾始安。

translations.literal: When the volunteer army was first established, popular feeling was turbulent; Zhaoshu rode post-horses traveling several stages a day, opened and instructed the elders, and the masses then settled.
translations.idiomatic: When the volunteer militia was first established, public unrest ran high; Zhaoshu rode post relays several stages a day, explained the policy to local elders, and the people calmed down.

sentences.zh: 宣撫使表其能，除龍圖閣直學士、知澶州，又為樞密直學士、陝西都轉運使。

translations.literal: The pacification commissioner memorialized his ability; he was made Dragon Diagram Hall academician, governor of Chanyuan, then also Privy Council academician and overall Shaanxi transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification commissioner praised his ability; he was made a Dragon Diagram Hall academician and governor of Chanyuan, then also a privy council academician and overall Shaanxi transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 河北始置四路，以為真定府路安撫使、知成德軍。

translations.literal: When Hebei first established four circuits, he was made pacification commissioner of the Zhending circuit and military governor of Chengde.
translations.idiomatic: When Hebei was first divided into four circuits, he was made pacification commissioner of the Zhending circuit and military governor of Chengde.

sentences.zh: 大水，民多流亡，籍僧舍積粟為粥糜，活饑民數萬計。

translations.literal: Great floods; many people fled. He requisitioned grain stored in monasteries to make gruel and porridge, saving tens of thousands of starving people.
translations.idiomatic: After severe flooding drove masses of people from their homes, he drew on grain stored in monasteries to make gruel and porridge, saving tens of thousands from starvation.

sentences.zh: 改龍圖閣學士、知秦州。

translations.literal: Changed to Dragon Diagram Hall scholar and governor of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Dragon Diagram Hall scholar and governor of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 諫官、御史言昭述庸懦，不可負重鎮，留真定府。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials and censors said Zhaoshu was mediocre and timid, unfit to bear a great commandery, and he was kept at Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials and censors said Zhaoshu was mediocre and timid and unfit for a major frontier post, so he was kept at Zhending.

sentences.zh: 居四年，入領三班院，以翰林侍讀學士知鄭州。

translations.literal: After four years he entered to head the Three Ranks Bureau, and as Hanlin attendant reader academician governed Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After four years he returned to the capital to head the Three Ranks Bureau and governed Zhengzhou as a Hanlin attendant reader academician.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知通進銀臺司，判太常寺，復領三班，累遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Before long he directed the Communication and Memorials Bureau, judged the Grand Secretariat, again headed the Three Ranks, and was repeatedly promoted to Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he directed the Communication and Memorials Bureau, served as judge of the Grand Secretariat, again headed the Three Ranks, and rose to right vice director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 從祫享致齋於朝堂，得暴疾卒。

translations.literal: While observing fast for the joint ancestral offering in the court hall, he contracted a sudden illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: While observing the fast for the joint ancestral offering in the court hall, he was struck by a sudden illness and died.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書，諡恪。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Minister of Rites; posthumous title Ke.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Rites, with the posthumous title Ke.

sentences.zh: 李氏居京城北崇慶里，凡七世不異爨，至昭述稍自豐殖，為族人所望，然家法亦不隳。

translations.literal: The Li clan lived in Chongqing Lane north of the capital; for seven generations they did not separate their cooking fires. By Zhaoshu's time they had grown somewhat prosperous and were looked to by the clan, yet the family rules were not destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The Li clan lived in Chongqing Lane north of the capital; for seven generations they had shared one kitchen. Zhaoshu brought the family modest prosperity and became the clan's pillar, yet its household discipline remained intact.

sentences.zh: 孫 昭遘

translations.literal: Grandson: Zhaoyao
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Zhaoyao

sentences.zh: 昭遘，字逢吉，宗諤從子也，以蔭為將作監主簿。

translations.literal: Zhaoyao, styled Fengji, was Zong'e's nephew; through privilege he became chief clerk of the Directorate of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyao, styled Fengji, was Zong'e's nephew; he entered office through privilege as chief clerk of the Directorate of Works.

sentences.zh: 幼時，楊億嘗過其家，出拜，億命為賦，既成，億曰：「桂林之下無雜木，非虛言也。

translations.literal: In youth Yang Yi once visited his home; he came out to bow. Yi ordered him to compose a fu; when it was done Yi said: "Under the osmanthus grove there are no stray trees—this is no empty saying.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Yang Yi once visited his home; Zhaoyao came out to pay his respects, and Yi asked him to compose a fu. When it was finished Yi said, "Under the osmanthus grove no stray tree grows—that old saying is no empty boast.

sentences.zh: 」其後薦之，召試，授館閣校勘，改集賢院校理。

translations.literal: " Later he recommended him; summoned to examination, he was given archive collator in the Institutes, then changed to collator of the Assembled Worthies Institute.
translations.idiomatic: " He later recommended him; called to examination, Zhaoyao was made an archive collator in the Institutes, then a collator of the Assembled Worthies Institute.

sentences.zh: 坐失誤落秩。

translations.literal: Because of an error he was demoted in rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted for an administrative error.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復為鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: Before long he was again made salt-and-iron administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored as salt-and-iron administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 初，議罷天下職田及公使錢，昭遘以為不可。

translations.literal: At first there was discussion of abolishing official fields and public envoy funds throughout the realm; Zhaoyao held that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the court first debated abolishing official fields and public envoy funds empire-wide, Zhaoyao argued against it.

sentences.zh: 三司使姚仲孫惡其異己，請詰所以興利之實，昭遘爭不屈，遂罷判官，為白波發運使。

translations.literal: Three Departments commissioner Yao Zhongsun hated his dissent, requested interrogation on the facts of how he increased profit; Zhaoyao argued and would not yield, and was therefore dismissed as administrative aide and made Baibo grain dispatch commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Three Departments commissioner Yao Zhongsun resented his opposition and demanded he prove how he would increase revenue; Zhaoyao refused to yield and was removed as administrative aide and posted as Baibo grain dispatch commissioner.

sentences.zh: 因入奏事，仁宗謂曰：「前所論罷職田等事，卿言是也。

translations.literal: When he entered to report affairs, Renzong said to him: "On the earlier matter of abolishing official fields and the like, your words were correct.
translations.idiomatic: On entering to report affairs, Renzong told him, "On the earlier proposal to abolish official fields and the like, you were right.

sentences.zh: 」遷直史館、知陝州。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Drafter of the Historiography Institute and governor of Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made a drafter of the Historiography Institute and governor of Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 諫官歐陽修言：「陝府，關中要地，昭遘無治劇材，不宜遣。

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Ouyang Xiu said: "Shaan Prefecture is a key place in the Guanzhong region; Zhaoyao lacks the talent to handle urgent affairs and should not be sent.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Ouyang Xiu said, "Shaan Prefecture is a vital post in the Guanzhong heartland; Zhaoyao lacks the talent for demanding administration and should not be sent there.

sentences.zh: 」改判三司理欠司，徙度支判官。

translations.literal: " He was changed to judge the Three Departments Arrears Bureau and moved to fiscal administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: " He was reassigned to judge the Three Departments Arrears Bureau and made a fiscal administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 使契丹還，道除陝西轉運使。

translations.literal: Returning from an embassy to the Khitan, he was appointed on the road as Shaanxi transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On his return from an embassy to the Khitan, he was appointed Shaanxi transport commissioner while still on the road.

sentences.zh: 坐家僮盜遼人銀酒杯，降知澤州。

translations.literal: Because a household servant stole a Liao man's silver wine cup, he was demoted to governor of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a household servant stole a Khitan envoy's silver wine cup, he was demoted to governor of Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 陽城冶鑄鐵錢，民冒山險輸礦炭，苦其役，為奏罷鑄錢。

translations.literal: In Yangcheng they cast iron coin; the people risked mountain perils to deliver ore and charcoal and suffered under the labor; he memorialized to stop coin casting.
translations.idiomatic: At Yangcheng the government cast iron coin; commoners braved mountain trails hauling ore and charcoal and groaned under the corvée; he memorialized to halt the mint.

sentences.zh: 又言：「河東鐵錢真偽淆雜，不可不革。」

translations.literal: He also said: "In Hedong iron coin true and false are mixed in confusion; this cannot go unreformed."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "In Hedong genuine and counterfeit iron coin circulate together; this abuse must be reformed."

sentences.zh: 後復直史館、知陝州。

translations.literal: Later he was again made Drafter of the Historiography Institute and governor of Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was again made a drafter of the Historiography Institute and governor of Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 城中舊無井，唐武德中，刺史長孫操始疏廣濟渠水入城，眾賴其利。

translations.literal: Within the city there were originally no wells; in the Wude era of Tang, prefect Zhangsun Cao first dredged the Guangji Canal water into the city, and the multitude relied on its benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The city had once had no wells; in Tang Wude reign the prefect Zhangsun Cao first led Guangji Canal water into the city, on which the people had long depended.

sentences.zh: 昭遘至，立廟祠之。

translations.literal: When Zhaoyao arrived, he established a shrine to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: On his arrival Zhaoyao erected a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 歸為三司戶部判官，糾察在京刑獄，進直龍圖閣，改集賢殿修撰，累遷尚書工部郎中。

translations.literal: On return he became Three Departments household administrative aide, inspected capital criminal prisons, advanced to Dragon Diagram Hall drafter, changed to Assembled Worthies Hall compiler, and was repeatedly promoted to Ministry of Works director.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he became a Three Departments household administrative aide, inspected capital criminal prisons, was promoted to Dragon Diagram Hall drafter, made a compiler of the Assembled Worthies Hall, and rose to director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 歷知鳳翔、河中府、晉州，遷管勾登聞檢院。

translations.literal: He successively governed Fengxiang, Hezhong Prefecture, and Jinzhou, and was moved to oversee the Memorials Inspection Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Fengxiang, Hezhong Prefecture, and Jinzhou in turn, then was put in charge of the Memorials Inspection Bureau.

sentences.zh: 擢天章閣待制、知滄州，用諫官吳及言，復改知陝州，徙鄭州卒。

translations.literal: Promoted to Tianzhang Hall attendant and governor of Cangzhou; following remonstrance official Wu Ji's words, he was again changed to governor of Shaanzhou, then moved to Zhengzhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Tianzhang Hall attendant and governor of Cangzhou; on remonstrance official Wu Ji's advice he was again made governor of Shaanzhou, then transferred to Zhengzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 昭遘性和易，不忤物，能守家法。

translations.literal: Zhaoyao's nature was easygoing; he did not offend others and could preserve the family rules.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyao was easygoing, gave no offense, and upheld the family discipline.

sentences.zh: 呂蒙正

translations.literal: Lü Mengzheng
translations.idiomatic: Lü Mengzheng

sentences.zh: 呂蒙正，字聖功，河南人。

translations.literal: Lü Mengzheng, styled Shenggong, a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Mengzheng, whose courtesy name was Shenggong, came from Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖夢奇，戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Grandfather Mengqi was Vice Minister of the Household Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mengqi had been vice minister of the household bureau.

sentences.zh: 父龜圖，起居郎。

translations.literal: Father Qitu was Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qitu had been an attendant gentleman.

sentences.zh: 蒙正，太平興國二年，擢進士第一，授將作監丞，通判昇州。

translations.literal: Mengzheng, in the second year of Taiping xingguo, was placed first among jinshi, appointed Director of Works aide, and made vice commissioner of Sheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping xingguo, Mengzheng took first place among the jinshi, was appointed an aide in the Directorate of Works, and made vice commissioner of Sheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，有旨，民事有不便者，許騎置以聞，賜錢二十萬。

translations.literal: At court farewell, there was an order that wherever civil affairs were inconvenient, he was permitted to use post relays to report, and he was given two hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience he was told that wherever civil affairs proved inconvenient he might use post relays to report it, and he was granted two hundred thousand in cash.

sentences.zh: 代還，會征太原，召見行在，授著作郎、直史館，加左拾遺。
