translations.idiomatic: Once the southwest has received orders and the border power is extended, then the shallow Fan of Bian, Yan, Huan, and Qing, and the registered households of Yuan, Wei, and Zhenrong, will naturally submit.

sentences.zh: 然後使之與對替甲兵及駐泊軍馬互為聲援，則萬山聞之，必不敢於靈州、河西頓兵矣。

translations.literal: Then have them mutually support the relief troops and stationed army horses, and when Mount Wan hears of it they will surely not dare to mass troops at Ling Prefecture and west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Then have them mutually support the relief troops and stationed army horses, and when Mount Wan hears of it they will surely not dare to mass troops at Ling Prefecture and west of the river.

sentences.zh: 萬山既退，則賀蘭蕃部亦稍稍叛繼遷矣。

translations.literal: Once Mount Wan has withdrawn, then the Helan Fan tribes will also gradually turn against Jiqian.
translations.idiomatic: Once Mount Wan has withdrawn, then the Helan Fan tribes will also gradually turn against Jiqian.

sentences.zh: 若曰名器不可以假人，爵賞不可以濫及，此乃聖人為治之常道，非隨時變易之義也。」

translations.literal: If one says titles and vessels may not be lent to others and enfeoffments and rewards may not be lavished indiscriminately—this is the sage's constant way in governing, not the meaning of changing with the times."
translations.idiomatic: If one says titles and vessels may not be lent to others and enfeoffments and rewards may not be lavished indiscriminately—this is the sage's constant way in governing, not the meaning of changing with the times."

sentences.zh: 齊賢又請調江淮、荊湘丁壯八萬以益防禦，朝議以為動搖，兼澤國人民，遠戍西鄙亦非便，計遂寢。

translations.literal: Qixian also requested that eight hundred thousand able-bodied men from Jianghuai and Jing-Hu be transferred to strengthen defense; court discussion held this would cause disturbance, and moreover the people of marsh lands, sent far to garrison the western marches, was also not convenient—the plan was then abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Qixian also requested that eight hundred thousand able-bodied men from Jianghuai and Jing-Hu be transferred to strengthen defense. Court discussion held this would cause disturbance, and moreover the people of marsh lands, sent far to garrison the western marches, was also not convenient, and the plan was then abandoned.

sentences.zh: 齊賢又言：「靈州斗絕一隅，當城鎮完全、磧路未梗之時，中外已言合棄，自繼遷為患已來，危困彌甚。

translations.literal: Qixian also said: "Ling Prefecture stands isolated at a corner. When the city defenses were complete and the desert road unobstructed, within and without already spoke of abandoning it together. Since Jiqian became a calamity, peril has grown ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: Qixian also said, "Ling Prefecture stands isolated at a corner. When the city defenses were complete and the desert road unobstructed, within and without already spoke of abandoning it together. Since Jiqian became a calamity, peril has grown ever worse.

sentences.zh: 南去鎮戎約五百餘里，東去環州僅六七日程，如此畏途，不須攻奪，則城中之民何由而出，城中之兵何由而歸？

translations.literal: South to Zhenrong is about five hundred-odd li; east to Huan Prefecture is only six or seven days' journey. On such a fearful road, without needing to attack and seize, how can the people within the city get out, how can the troops within the city return?
translations.idiomatic: South to Zhenrong is about five hundred-odd li; east to Huan Prefecture is only six or seven days' journey. On such a fearful road, without needing to attack and seize, how can the people within the city get out, how can the troops within the city return?

sentences.zh: 欲全軍民，理須應接。

translations.literal: To preserve army and people entirely, reason requires that they be supported.
translations.idiomatic: To preserve army and people entirely, reason requires that they be supported.

sentences.zh: 為今之計，若能增益精兵，以合西邊屯駐、對替之兵，從以原、渭、鎮戎之師，率山西熟戶從東界而入，嚴約師期，兩路交進。

translations.literal: For the plan of today, if elite troops can be increased to join the western border garrisons and relief troops, accompanied by the armies of Yuan, Wei, and Zhenrong, leading registered households of the western mountains to enter from the eastern boundary, with strict agreement on army dates and two routes advancing together—
translations.idiomatic: For the plan of today, if elite troops can be increased to join the western border garrisons and relief troops, accompanied by the armies of Yuan, Wei, and Zhenrong, leading registered households of the western mountains to enter from the eastern boundary, with strict agreement on army dates and two routes advancing together,

sentences.zh: 設若繼遷分兵以應敵，我則乘勢而易攻。

translations.literal: Suppose Jiqian divides troops to meet the enemy—we then take advantage of the situation for easy attack.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose Jiqian divides troops to meet the enemy—we then take advantage of the situation for easy attack.

sentences.zh: 且奔命途道，首尾難衛，千里趨利，不敗則禽。

translations.literal: Moreover, racing orders along the road, head and tail hard to guard, rushing a thousand li for profit—if not defeated then captured.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, racing orders along the road, head and tail hard to guard, rushing a thousand li for profit—if not defeated then captured.

sentences.zh: 臣謂兵鋒未交，而靈州之圍自解。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that before the army's edge has met, the siege of Ling Prefecture will resolve itself.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that before the army's edge has met, the siege of Ling Prefecture will resolve itself.

sentences.zh: 然後取靈州軍民，而置砦於蕭關、武延川險要處以僑寓之，如此則蕃漢士人之心有所依賴。

translations.literal: Then take the troops and people of Ling Prefecture and place forts at the strategic points of Xiaoguan and Wuyan River to lodge them temporarily—thus the hearts of Fan and Han scholars and people will have something to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Then take the troops and people of Ling Prefecture and place forts at the strategic points of Xiaoguan and Wuyan River to lodge them temporarily—thus the hearts of Fan and Han scholars and people will have something to rely on.

sentences.zh: 裁候平寧，卻歸舊貫，然後縱蕃漢之兵，乘時以為進退，則成功不難矣。

translations.literal: Trim the season until peace and quiet, then return to the old practice; afterward release Fan and Han troops and take opportunity for advance and retreat—then success is not hard."
translations.idiomatic: Trim the season until peace and quiet, then return to the old practice. Afterward release Fan and Han troops and take opportunity for advance and retreat—then success is not hard."

sentences.zh: 」時不能用。

translations.literal: " At the time it could not be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time it could not be adopted.

sentences.zh: 未幾，靈武果陷。

translations.literal: Before long Lingwu indeed fell.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Lingwu indeed fell.

sentences.zh: 閏十二月，拜右僕射、判邠州，不行，改判永興軍兼馬步軍部署。

translations.literal: In the intercalary twelfth month he was appointed Right Vice Director and judge of Bin Prefecture; he did not go and was changed to judge of Yongxing Army concurrently with Commissioner of Cavalry and Infantry.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary twelfth month he was appointed Right Vice Director and judge of Bin Prefecture. He did not go and was changed to judge of Yongxing Army concurrently with Commissioner of Cavalry and Infantry.

sentences.zh: 時薛居正子惟吉妻柴氏無子早寡，盡畜其貨產及書籍論告，欲改適齊賢。

translations.literal: At the time Xue Juzheng's son Weiji's wife, the Chai clan, was without a son and widowed early; she stored all her property and books and memorialized accusations, wishing to remarry Qixian.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xue Juzheng's son Weiji's wife, the Chai clan, was without a son and widowed early. She stored all her property and books and memorialized accusations, wishing to remarry Qixian.

sentences.zh: 惟吉子安上訴其事，上不欲置於理，命司門員外郎張正倫就訊，柴氏所對與安上狀異。

translations.literal: Weiji's son An appealed the matter; the emperor did not wish to place it in the law courts and ordered Vice Director of the Gate Office Zhang Zhenglun to conduct an inquiry on the spot. The Chai clan's answers differed from An's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Weiji's son An appealed the matter. The emperor did not wish to place it in the law courts and ordered Vice Director of the Gate Office Zhang Zhenglun to conduct an inquiry on the spot. The Chai clan's answers differed from An's memorial.

sentences.zh: 下其事於御史，乃齊賢子太子中舍宗誨教柴氏為詞。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the censorate—it was Qixian's son, Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household Zonghui, who had taught the Chai clan her words.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was sent down to the censorate—it was Qixian's son, Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household Zonghui, who had taught the Chai clan her words.

sentences.zh: 齊賢坐責太常卿、分司西京，宗誨貶海州別駕。

translations.literal: Qixian was punished by demotion to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and commissioner in the Western Capital, and Zonghui was demoted to Assistant Prefect of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qixian was punished by demotion to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and commissioner in the Western Capital, and Zonghui was demoted to Assistant Prefect of Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 景德初，起為兵部尚書、知青州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he was raised as Vice Minister of War and prefect of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jingde he was raised as Vice Minister of War and prefect of Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 上幸澶淵，命兼青、淄、濰州安撫使。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Chanyuan he was ordered concurrently to be Pacification Commissioner of Qing, Zi, and Wei prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Chanyuan he was ordered concurrently to be Pacification Commissioner of Qing, Zi, and Wei prefectures.

sentences.zh: 二年，改吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year he was changed to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was changed to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 上疏言曰：「 臣在先朝，常憂靈、夏，兩鎮終為繼遷並吞，言事者以臣所慮為太過，略舉既往之事以明本末。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "During the previous reign, your servant often worried that the two prefectures of Ling and Xia would in the end be swallowed and annexed by Jiqian. Those who spoke on state affairs regarded what your servant feared as going too far. I shall briefly cite past events to make clear the beginning and end."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qixian submitted a memorial that read: "In the previous reign I often feared that Lingzhou and Xiazhou would ultimately be absorbed by Li Jiqian. Officials who addressed policy matters thought my concern excessive. I will briefly recount what has already happened to show how matters unfolded from start to finish."

sentences.zh: 當時臣下皆以繼遷只是懷戀父祖舊地，別無他心，先帝與以銀州廉察，庶滿其意。

translations.literal: At that time all officials held that Jiqian merely longed for his father's and grandfather's old territory and had no other intent. The former emperor gave him the inspectorate of Yin Prefecture, hoping thereby to satisfy his wishes.
translations.idiomatic: At the time every official maintained that Jiqian wanted only his ancestors' former lands and harbored no wider ambition. The late emperor gave him the Yinzhou inspectorate, hoping that would satisfy him.

sentences.zh: 爾後攻劫不已，直至降麟、府州界八部族蕃酋，又脅制賀蘭山下帳族，言事者猶謂封獎未厚。

translations.literal: Thereafter raids and plunder never ceased, until he had reduced the eight tribal chiefs of the border between Lin and Fu prefectures to submission, and again coerced the tent-dwelling tribes below Helan Mountain. Those who spoke on affairs still said enfeoffment and reward had not been generous enough.
translations.idiomatic: After that he raided without cease, subduing the eight tribal chiefs along the Linzhou-Fuzhou frontier and coercing the tent peoples below Helan Mountain. Memorialists still argued that his titles and rewards had not been generous enough.

sentences.zh: 洎陛下賜以銀、夏土壤，寵以節旄，自此姦威愈滋，逆志尤暴。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty then bestowed on him the lands of Yin and Xia and honored him with a military commissioner's baton and banner, from that point his treacherous power grew ever greater and his rebellious will grew all the more violent.
translations.idiomatic: Once Your Majesty granted him Yinzhou and Xiazhou and invested him with a commissioner's insignia, his treachery grew only stronger and his defiance far fiercer.

sentences.zh: 屢斷靈州糧路，復撓緣邊城池，數年之間，靈州終為吞噬。

translations.literal: He repeatedly severed Lingzhou's grain routes and again harassed frontier fortresses and cities. Within a few years Lingzhou was finally devoured.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly cut Lingzhou's supply lines and harassed border towns until, within a few years, the prefecture fell entirely into his hands.

sentences.zh: 當靈池、清遠軍垂欲陷沒，臣方受經略之命。

translations.literal: When Ling Pool and Qingyuan Army were on the verge of being overrun and lost, your servant had just received the command of frontier administration.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingchi and the Qingyuan garrison were on the brink of collapse, I had just been assigned to oversee the frontier.

sentences.zh: 臣思繼遷須是得一兩處強大蕃族與之為敵，此乃以蠻夷攻蠻夷，古今之上策也。

translations.literal: Your servant reflected that Jiqian necessarily had to obtain one or two powerful Fan tribes as his enemies. This is using the barbarians to attack the barbarians—the supreme stratagem of antiquity and the present.
translations.idiomatic: I reasoned that Jiqian could be checked only if one or two powerful tribal groups were set against him—the classic strategy of pitting barbarian against barbarian.

sentences.zh: 遂請以六谷名目封潘羅支，俾其展效。

translations.literal: Thereupon he requested that Pan Luozhi be enfeoffed under the title of Six Valleys, so that he might display his merit in service.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore asked that Pan Luozhi be enfeoffed under the Six Valleys title so that he could act against Jiqian.

sentences.zh: 其時近臣所見，全與臣謀不同，多為沮撓。

translations.literal: At that time the views of nearby ministers were entirely unlike your servant's plan, and many obstructed and blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers close to the throne saw things altogether differently and largely blocked the proposal.

sentences.zh: 及繼遷為潘羅支射殺，邊患謂可少息。

translations.literal: When Jiqian was shot and killed by Pan Luozhi, the frontier calamity was thought able to subside somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: After Pan Luozhi killed Jiqian with an arrow, the frontier crisis was thought to ease at last.

sentences.zh: 今其子德明依前攻劫，析逋遊龍缽等盡在部下，其志又似不小。

translations.literal: Now his son Deming, as before, raids and plunders; Xibo, Youlongbo, and the like are all under his command, and his intent again seems no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: Now his son Deming raids as before. Tribal leaders such as Xibo and Youlongbo are all in his following, and his designs again appear ambitious.

sentences.zh: 臣慮德明乘大駕東幸之際，去攻六谷，則瓜、沙、甘、肅、于闐諸處漸為控制矣。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that Deming, taking advantage of the occasion when the imperial carriage proceeds east on the Fengshan journey, may go attack Six Valleys; then Guazhou, Shazhou, Ganzhou, Suzhou, Khotan, and the like would gradually come under his control.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that while the imperial progress is in the east, Deming may strike at the Six Valleys and then gradually bring Guazhou, Shazhou, Ganzhou, Suzhou, Khotan, and the rest under his control.

sentences.zh: 向使潘羅支尚在，則德明未足為虞；

translations.literal: Had Pan Luozhi still been alive, then Deming would not have been worth worrying over;
translations.idiomatic: Had Pan Luozhi still lived, Deming would scarcely have been cause for alarm;

sentences.zh: 今潘羅支已亡，廝鐸督恐非其敵。

translations.literal: now Pan Luozhi is already dead, and Sieduoge probably is not his match.
translations.idiomatic: but Pan Luozhi is dead, and Sieduoge is probably no match for him.

sentences.zh: 望委大臣經制其事。」

translations.literal: Your servant hopes that major ministers may be charged to plan and control this matter."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that senior ministers be assigned to handle the matter."

sentences.zh: 從東封還，復拜右僕射。

translations.literal: When he returned from the eastern Fengshan, he was again appointed Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from the eastern Fengshan rites, he was again appointed Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時建玉清昭應宮，齊賢言繪畫符瑞，有損謙德，又違奉天之意，屢請罷其役。

translations.literal: At the time the Jade Pure Palace of Manifest Response was being built. Qixian said that painting auspicious omens and prodigies would impair modest virtue and also contravene the meaning of honoring Heaven. He repeatedly requested that the work be halted.
translations.idiomatic: While the Jade Pure Palace of Manifest Response was under construction, Qixian argued that painting omens and prodigies would diminish modest virtue and violate the spirit of honoring Heaven. He repeatedly asked that the project be stopped.

sentences.zh: 三年，出判河陽，從祀汾陰還，進左僕射。

translations.literal: In the third year he was sent out as administrative prefect of Heyang. After returning from the Fengyin sacrifice he was promoted to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was posted as administrative prefect of Heyang. After accompanying the Fengyin sacrifice he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五年，代還，請老，以司空致仕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when his replacement arrived, he requested retirement and was granted privilege to retire with the title of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his successor arrived; he asked to retire and was permitted to withdraw with the rank of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 入辭便坐，方拜而仆，上遽止之，許二子扶掖升殿，命益坐茵為三。

translations.literal: On entering to take leave at the Informal Audience, he had just begun to bow when he collapsed. The emperor hastily stopped him, permitted his two sons to support him up onto the dais, and ordered that cushion-pads be increased to three.
translations.idiomatic: When he came in to bid farewell at the Informal Audience, he had barely begun to bow when he fell. The emperor quickly stopped him, allowed his two sons to help him onto the dais, and ordered a third cushion placed for him to sit on.

sentences.zh: 歸洛，得裴度午橋莊，有池榭松竹之盛，日與親舊觴詠其間，意甚曠適。

translations.literal: Returning to Luoyang, he obtained Pei Du's Noon Bridge estate, with its splendid pools, pavilions, pines, and bamboo. Day after day he drank and composed verse there with kin and old friends, his mind very free and at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Luoyang he acquired Pei Du's Noon Bridge estate, with its fine pools, pavilions, pines, and bamboo. There he drank and wrote poetry daily with relatives and old friends, his spirit altogether serene and free.

sentences.zh: 七年夏，薨，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the seventh summer he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, summer, he died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒，諡文定。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Minister of Education, with posthumous title Wending ("Cultivated and Steady").
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Education and given the posthumous title Wending, "Cultivated and Settled."

sentences.zh: 齊賢姿儀豐碩，議論慷慨，有大略，以致君自負。

translations.literal: Qixian's bearing and appearance were ample and imposing; his discourse was ardent and generous. He possessed great strategic vision and took pride in bringing his lord to accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: Qixian was imposing in stature and voice, spoke with force and breadth, and held to a grand design, confident that he could guide his sovereign to success.

sentences.zh: 留心刑獄，多所全活。

translations.literal: He paid close attention to penal cases and preserved many lives.
translations.idiomatic: He took a close interest in criminal justice and saved many from execution.

sentences.zh: 喜提獎寒雋。

translations.literal: He delighted in lifting up talented men of modest background.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in promoting talented men of humble origin.

sentences.zh: 少時家貧，父死無以為葬，河南縣吏為辦其事，齊賢深德之，事以兄禮，雖貴不替也。

translations.literal: When young his family was poor. When his father died there was no means to bury him; a clerk of Henan County arranged the funeral. Qixian was deeply grateful and treated him with the courtesy due an elder brother—a practice he never abandoned even after rising high.
translations.idiomatic: In youth his family was poor. When his father died he could not afford a burial until a clerk of Henan County arranged it. Qixian never forgot the debt and treated the man as an elder brother, a courtesy he kept even at the height of his career.

sentences.zh: 仲兄昭度嘗授齊賢經，及卒，表贈光祿寺丞。

translations.literal: His elder brother Zhaodu had once taught Qixian the classics. When he died, Qixian memorialized for him the posthumous gift of Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Zhaodu had once taught him the classics. When Zhaodu died, Qixian memorialized for him a posthumous appointment as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 又嘗依太子少師李肅家，肅死，為營葬事，歲時祭之。

translations.literal: He had also once relied on the household of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Li Su. When Su died, Qixian arranged his burial and offered seasonal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He had also once lived under the roof of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Li Su. When Su died, Qixian arranged his burial and made seasonal offerings thereafter.

sentences.zh: 趙普嘗薦齊賢於太宗，未用，普即具前列事，以謂：「陛下若進齊賢，則齊賢他日感恩，更過於此。

translations.literal: Zhao Pu once recommended Qixian to Taizong, but he was not employed. Pu then set forth in full the preceding matters and said: "If Your Majesty advances Qixian, then when Qixian one day feels gratitude, it will exceed even this."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Pu once recommended Qixian to Emperor Taizong, but the appointment was not made. Pu then laid out in full what he had done for Qixian and said, "If Your Majesty promotes Qixian now, his gratitude one day will exceed even this."

sentences.zh: 」上大悅，遂大用。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and thereafter employed him to the full.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and thereafter gave him full employment.

sentences.zh: 种放之起，齊賢所薦也。

translations.literal: Chong Fang's rise to office was through Qixian's recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Chong Fang's rise to prominence came through Qixian's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 齊賢四踐兩府，九居八座，以三公就第，康寧福壽，時罕其比。

translations.literal: Qixian four times entered the Two Departments, nine times held one of the Eight Seats, and retired to his residence with the rank of Three Excellencies—healthy, tranquil, blessed, and long-lived; in his day few could be compared with him.
translations.idiomatic: Qixian served four times in the Two Departments, nine times among the Eight Seats, and retired home with the rank of the Three Excellencies—healthy, secure, blessed, and long-lived, a combination rare in his age.

sentences.zh: 居相日，數起大獄，又與寇準相傾，人或以此少之。

translations.literal: While serving as chief minister he repeatedly launched major prosecutions and also clashed with Kou Zhun; some therefore thought somewhat less of him.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister he repeatedly opened major prosecutions and also feuded with Kou Zhun, and some held that against him.

sentences.zh: 齊賢諸子皆能有立：宗信，內殿崇班；

translations.literal: All Qixian's sons were able to make their mark: Zongxin, Inner Hall Honored Escort;
translations.idiomatic: All of Qixian's sons made their way in the world: Zongxin became an Inner Hall Honored Escort;

sentences.zh: 宗理，大理寺丞；

translations.literal: Zongli, Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review;
translations.idiomatic: Zongli, Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review;

sentences.zh: 宗諒，殿中丞；

translations.literal: Zongliang, Director Within the Hall;
translations.idiomatic: Zongliang, Director Within the Hall;

sentences.zh: 宗簡，閣門祗候；

translations.literal: Zongjian, Gate Attendant of the Imperial Portal;
translations.idiomatic: Zongjian, Gate Attendant of the Imperial Portal;

sentences.zh: 宗訥，太子中舍；

translations.literal: Zongne, Rectifier of the Heir Apparent's Household;
translations.idiomatic: Zongne, Rectifier of the Heir Apparent's Household;

sentences.zh: 宗禮最賢，雖累資登朝，而畏羈束，故多居田里。

translations.literal: Zongli was the most worthy. Though through accumulated qualification he took court office, he feared restraint and therefore often remained in the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Zongli was the most worthy of them. Though seniority eventually brought him to court, he disliked constraint and mostly lived in the countryside.

sentences.zh: 子 宗誨

translations.literal: Son: Zonghui
translations.idiomatic: Son: Zonghui

sentences.zh: 宗誨，字習之，齊賢第二子也。

translations.literal: Zonghui, style Xizhi, was Qixian's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghui, styled Xizhi, was Qixian's second son.

sentences.zh: 少喜學兵法，陰陽、象緯之書無不通究。

translations.literal: In youth he delighted in studying military methods and thoroughly mastered books on yin-yang, astral omens, and celestial coordinates.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved military science and mastered works on cosmology, divination, and astronomy alike.

sentences.zh: 以父蔭為秘書省正字，遷至太子中舍，貶海州別駕。

translations.literal: Through his father's privilege he became Corrector in the Secretariat; he rose to Rectifier of the Heir Apparent's Household and was demoted to Vice Prefect of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's privilege he entered service as a Secretariat corrector, rose to Rectifier of the Heir Apparent's Household, and was demoted to Vice Prefect of Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗通判河陽，徙知富順監。

translations.literal: He once served as transit judge of Heyang and was transferred to administer the Fushun Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He once served as transit judge of Heyang and was later transferred to head the Fushun Directorate.

sentences.zh: 會夷人斗郎春叛，群獠皆騷動，宗誨將郡兵攻破之。

translations.literal: When the Yi chieftain Doulangchun rebelled and the mass of Liao tribes were all in turmoil, Zonghui led prefectural troops and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yi leader Doulangchun rebelled and tribal groups across the region rose in unrest, Zonghui led prefectural troops and broke the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 擢開封府判官、三司度支勾院。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Administrative Judge of the Kaifeng Prefectural Court and to the Audit Office of the Three Departments' Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to administrative judge of the Kaifeng prefectural court and to the audit office of the Three Departments' revenue section.

sentences.zh: 宗誨在開封日，御史王沿劾其嗜酒廢事，及為河北轉運使，乃發沿居喪假官舟賈販，朝論惡之。

translations.literal: While Zonghui was in Kaifeng, Censor Wang Yan impeached him for loving wine and neglecting duties. When he became transport commissioner of Hebei, he exposed that during mourning Yan had used an official boat for trade. Court opinion turned against him.
translations.idiomatic: While Zonghui was in Kaifeng, Censor Wang Yan impeached him for drinking to excess and neglecting his duties. Once Zonghui became Hebei transport commissioner, he exposed Yan's use of an official boat for trade during mourning, and court opinion turned against him.

sentences.zh: 會以調發擾民，徙知徐州。

translations.literal: Because requisition and dispatch disturbed the people, he was transferred to administer Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his requisitions burdened the people, he was transferred to administer Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 累遷太常少卿，後為永興軍兵馬鈐轄，又徙鄜延路兼知鄜州。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, later Military Controller of Yongxing Army, and again was transferred to the Yan-Yan Circuit while also administering Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then served as military controller of Yongxing Army, and was later transferred to the Yan-Yan circuit while also governing Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元昊寇延安，劉平、石元孫敗沒，鈐轄黃德和遁還，延州不納，又走鄜州。

translations.literal: Yuanhao raided Yan'an. Liu Ping and Shi Yuansun were defeated and lost. Military Controller Huang Dehe fled back; Yan Prefecture would not admit him, and he again fled to Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao attacked Yan'an, Liu Ping and Shi Yuansun were defeated and lost. Military Controller Huang Dehe fled back, but Yanzhou refused him entry, so he fled on to Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宗誨曰：「軍奔將無所歸，激之則為亂矣。

translations.literal: Zonghui said: "When troops flee and a general has nowhere to go, if you provoke him he will become a source of disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Zonghui said, "When routed troops have nowhere to go, a general with no refuge, if you push him further you will breed mutiny."

sentences.zh: 」乃納之，拘德和以聞。

translations.literal: Thereupon he admitted him, detained Dehe, and reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore admitted Dehe, detained him, and reported the matter to the court.

sentences.zh: 是時鄜城不完，且無備，傳言寇兵至，人心不安。

translations.literal: At that time the walls of Yan city were incomplete and there was no defense. Rumor spread that enemy troops had arrived, and hearts were unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the walls of Yan were unfinished and the city unprepared. Rumors of approaching raiders unsettled the populace.

sentences.zh: 宗誨乃嚴斥候，籍入而禁出，使老幼倂力守禦之，敵亦自引去。

translations.literal: Zonghui then tightened scouts and patrols, registered entrants and forbade departures, and made old and young alike join in defense. The enemy also withdrew of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghui tightened scouting, registered those entering and barred departures, and rallied young and old to defend together. The enemy withdrew on their own.

sentences.zh: 領興州防禦使，復徙永興鈐轄兼知邠州，以秘書監致仕。

translations.literal: He held the post of Defender of Xing Prefecture, was again transferred as Military Controller of Yongxing while also administering Bin Prefecture, and retired with the title of Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Defender of Xing Prefecture, was again made military controller of Yongxing while also governing Bin Prefecture, and retired with the rank of Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 嘗事干謁，其子曰：「昔賀秘監以道士服東歸會稽，明皇賜以鑒湖，以為休老之地。

translations.literal: He had once gone about soliciting favors. His son said: "In the past, Junior Mentor He, wearing Taoist robes, returned east to Kuaiji; Emperor Ming bestowed Mirror Lake on him as a place to rest in old age."
translations.idiomatic: He had once gone about seeking favors. His son said, "Long ago Junior Mentor He Zhizhang, dressed as a Daoist, returned east to Kuaiji, and Emperor Xuanzong gave him Mirror Lake as a place to spend his old age."

sentences.zh: 今洛下雖無鑒湖，而嵩、少、伊，天下佳處，雖非朝廷所賜，皆閑逸之人所有爾。

translations.literal: Today below Luo there is no Mirror Lake, yet Song, Shao, and Yi are among the finest places under Heaven. Though not granted by the court, they all belong to men at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang may lack Mirror Lake, but Mount Song, Mount Shao, and the Yi River are among the finest places under Heaven. Though the court did not grant them, they belong to those who live at ease.

sentences.zh: 大人盍衣羽服以優遊，何必更事請謁乎？

translations.literal: Why does Father not don feathered robes and roam at ease? Why must he again pursue requests and audiences?
translations.idiomatic: Why not put on feathered robes and wander freely? Why go on begging audiences and favors?"

sentences.zh: 」宗誨曰：「吾作白頭老監秘書而眠，何以賀老流沙之服為哉？

translations.literal: Zonghui said: "Shall I put on flowing robes like Old He and sleep as a white-haired supervising secretary? What use have I for that?"
translations.idiomatic: Zonghui replied, "I am content to sleep out my days as a white-haired supervising secretary. What need have I for Old He's flowing robes from the western desert?"

sentences.zh: 」時以為名言。

translations.literal: At the time this was regarded as a saying worth remembering.
translations.idiomatic: At the time this was regarded as a memorable saying.

sentences.zh: 初，齊賢守代州，宗誨嘗預計畫，其保任親族不問疏近，以年為先後。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qixian guarded Dai Prefecture, Zonghui had once taken part in planning. In guaranteeing and appointing kin he did not distinguish near from distant, but took age as the order of precedence.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Qixian governed Dai Prefecture, Zonghui had helped plan policy. In recommending relatives for office he ignored degrees of kinship and ranked candidates by age alone.

sentences.zh: 然性貪，雖謝事，猶事貨殖，以至於卒。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was greedy. Though he had left office, he still pursued trade and profit until his death.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was greedy by nature and, even after leaving office, kept trading for profit until he died.

sentences.zh: 子二人。

translations.literal: He had two sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons.

sentences.zh: 子皋，字叔謨，少有才名而不自負，人樂與之遊。

translations.literal: Zigao, style Shumo, in youth had a reputation for talent yet did not pride himself on it. People delighted in associating with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zigao, styled Shumo, won an early name for talent without arrogance, and people were glad to keep his company.

sentences.zh: 最善尹洙，洙曰：「吾交天下士多矣，不以通否易意者，子皋也。

translations.literal: He was closest to Yin Zhu. Zhu said: "I have befriended gentlemen throughout the realm in great number; one who does not alter his regard according to success or failure is Zigao."
translations.idiomatic: He was closest to Yin Zhu, who said, "I have known scholars across the empire, but one whose regard does not shift with fortune or misfortune is Zigao."

sentences.zh: 」舉進士，試秘書郎、知新鄭縣。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was tried out as Secretariat Gentleman, and administered Xinzheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, served provisionally as Secretariat Gentleman, and governed Xinzheng County.

sentences.zh: 以齊賢相，遷校書郎，館閣獻頌，擢著作佐郎，進直史館，累官至尚書司封員外郎。

translations.literal: Because Qixian became chief minister, he was transferred to Collator. He presented a eulogy to the Academy and Library, was promoted to Assistant Compiler, advanced to duty in the Historiography Institute, and through accumulated offices reached Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites' Seals Section.
translations.idiomatic: When Qixian became chief minister, Zigao was moved to collator. A eulogy he offered to the Hanlin Academy won him promotion to Assistant Compiler, then appointment to the Historiography Institute, and eventually Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites' Seals Section.

sentences.zh: 子憲，字彥章，以蔭將作監主簿，以獻文賜同進士出身，累遷尚書刑部郎中、知光化軍。

translations.literal: Zixian, style Yanzhang, through privilege became Chief Clerk of the Directorate of Imperial Works. Through presenting a literary work he was granted jinshi status by imperial favor. Through successive promotions he became Director of the Ministry of Justice's Penal Section and administered Guanghua Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zixian, styled Yanzhang, entered service by privilege as chief clerk of the Directorate of Imperial Works. A literary submission earned him jinshi status by imperial favor. He rose to Director in the Ministry of Justice's Penal Section and governed Guanghua Army.

sentences.zh: 戍卒逐其帥韓綱，餘黨作亂，子憲招降之。

translations.literal: Garrison soldiers drove out their commander Han Gang; the remaining factions made trouble. Zixian induced them to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison expelled its commander Han Gang, and the remaining mutineers rose in disorder until Zixian persuaded them to surrender.

sentences.zh: 征稅重，人多逋負，子憲奏除之。

translations.literal: Tax levies were heavy and many people were in arrears. Zixian memorialized to abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes were heavy and many fell into arrears; Zixian memorialized to have them remitted.

sentences.zh: 歷太常少卿、三司鹽鐵判官、直史館、知洪州。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Administrative Judge of the Three Departments' Salt and Iron Section, duty officer in the Historiography Institute, and administrator of Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, salt-and-iron judge in the Three Departments, historian on duty in the Historiography Institute, and prefect of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷右諫議大夫、知桂州，不赴，御史劾之，降秘書監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Remonstrance Grandee and administrator of Gui Prefecture, but did not go. Censors impeached him and he was demoted to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Remonstrance Grandee and assigned to govern Guizhou, but did not take up the post. Censors impeached him and he was demoted to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 復為光祿卿，加直秘閣、知廬州，遷秘書監，累職徙揚州，卒。

translations.literal: He was again made Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, added duty in the Secret Archive, and administered Lu Prefecture. He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, and through accumulated offices was moved to Yang Prefecture, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored as Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, given duty in the Secret Archive, and made prefect of Luzhou. He was later made Director of the Secretariat, moved through several posts to Yangzhou, and died there.

sentences.zh: 賈黃中

translations.literal: Jia Huangzhong
translations.idiomatic: Jia Huangzhong

sentences.zh: 賈黃中，字媧民，滄州南皮人，唐相耽四世孫。

translations.literal: Jia Huangzhong, style Guamin, was a native of Nanpi in Cang Prefecture, fourth-generation descendant of Tang chief minister Jia Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Huangzhong, styled Guamin, was a native of Nanpi in Cangzhou, a fourth-generation descendant of the Tang chief minister Jia Dan.

sentences.zh: 父玭，字仲寶，晉天福三年進士，解褐。

translations.literal: His father Bin, style Zhongbao, passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Tianfu of Jin and left office dress for service.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bin, styled Zhongbao, passed the jinshi examination in the third year of the Later Jin Tianfu era and entered government service.

sentences.zh: 宋初，為刑部郎中，終水部員外郎、知浚儀縣，年七十卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was Director of the Ministry of Justice's Penal Section and ended as Vice Director of the Ministry of Works' Water Section and administrator of Junyi County, dying at seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he served as Director in the Ministry of Justice's Penal Section and ended his career as Vice Director in the Ministry of Works' Water Section and magistrate of Junyi County, dying at seventy.

sentences.zh: 玭嚴毅，善教子，士大夫子弟來謁，必諄諄誨誘之。

translations.literal: Bin was stern and resolute, skilled at teaching his sons. When sons of scholar-officials came to call, he unfailingly instructed and guided them with care.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was stern and disciplined, skilled at raising sons. Whenever the sons of scholar-officials called on him, he earnestly instructed and guided them.

sentences.zh: 初，通判鎮州，葬鄉黨群從之未葬者十五喪，孤貧不自給者，咸教育而婚嫁之。

translations.literal: Earlier, while transit judge of Zhen Prefecture, he buried fifteen coffins of kinsmen in the village and clan who had not yet been buried. Those orphaned and poor who could not support themselves, he all educated and provided marriage for.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as transit judge of Zhenzhou, he buried fifteen kinsmen of his village and clan who had gone unburied, and for orphans and the poor who could not support themselves he provided education and arranged marriages.

sentences.zh: 黃中幼聰悟，方五歲，比每旦令正立，展書卷比之，謂之「等身書」，課其誦讀。

translations.literal: Huangzhong in youth was clever and perceptive. When he was just five, Bin each morning made him stand straight, unrolled a book scroll and measured it against him, calling it a "body-height book," and set him to recite and read.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong was clever as a child. At five, each morning his father made him stand upright, unrolled a scroll to his height, called it a "body-length book," and drilled him in recitation.

sentences.zh: 六歲舉童子科，七歲能屬文，觸類賦詠。

translations.literal: At six he entered the Youth Examination; at seven he could compose prose and, on whatever subject arose, compose verse.
translations.idiomatic: At six he passed the Youth Examination; at seven he could write prose and compose verse on any theme set before him.

sentences.zh: 父常令蔬食，曰：「俟業成，乃得食肉。

translations.literal: His father often made him eat vegetables and said: "Wait until your studies are complete; only then may you eat meat."
translations.idiomatic: His father often fed him only vegetables, saying, "When your studies are finished, you may eat meat."

sentences.zh: 」十五舉進士，授校書郎、集賢校理，遷著作佐郎、直史館。

translations.literal: At fifteen he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Collator, and made Collating Editor in the Academy for Worthies; he was transferred to Assistant Compiler and duty in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed collator and collating editor in the Academy for Worthies, and was later made Assistant Compiler with duty in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，遷左拾遺，歷左補闕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong he was transferred to Left Reminder and passed through Left Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Jianlong era he was made Left Reminder and later served as Left Supplementation Censor.

sentences.zh: 開寶八年，通判定州，判太常禮院。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kaibao he was transit judge of Ding Prefecture and concurrently judged the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' Rites Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Kaibao era he served as transit judge of Dingzhou and concurrently oversaw the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' Rites Office.

sentences.zh: 黃中多識典故，每詳定禮文，損益得中，號為稱職。

translations.literal: Huangzhong knew many precedents and models. Whenever he examined and fixed ritual texts, additions and subtractions hit the mean, and he was acclaimed as fulfilling his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong knew a great store of precedent. Whenever he revised ritual texts his adjustments struck the right balance, and he was praised as thoroughly competent.

sentences.zh: 嶺南平，以黃中為采訪使，廉直平恕，遠人便之。

translations.literal: When Lingnan was pacified, Huangzhong was made Investigation Commissioner. Upright, fair, and forgiving, distant peoples found him convenient.
translations.idiomatic: After Lingnan was pacified, Huangzhong was made investigation commissioner. Honest, even-handed, and forgiving, he made life easier for the peoples of the far south.

sentences.zh: 還奏利害數十事，皆稱旨。

translations.literal: On returning he memorialized several tens of matters of benefit and harm, all of which accorded with the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he memorialized on dozens of matters of policy, all of which met with imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 會克江表，選知宣州。

translations.literal: When the region south of the Yangzi was taken, he was selected to administer Xuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the lower Yangzi region was conquered, he was chosen to govern Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，民多為盜，黃中出己奉造糜粥，賴全活者以千數，仍設法弭盜，因悉解去。

translations.literal: The year was famine-struck and many among the people became bandits. Huangzhong spent his own salary to make gruel and porridge; those who relied on it to survive numbered in the thousands. He also set up methods to quell banditry and thereby released them all.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine many turned to banditry. Huangzhong spent his own salary to provide gruel, saving thousands of lives, then devised measures to end the unrest and released the offenders.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，遷禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Huangzhong was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong ascended the throne, Huangzhong was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，知昇州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he administered Sheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Taiping Xingguo era he was made prefect of Shengzhou.

sentences.zh: 時金陵初附，黃中為政簡易，部內甚治。

translations.literal: At the time Jinling had just submitted. Huangzhong's governance was simple and easy, and within his jurisdiction there was great order.
translations.idiomatic: Jinling had only recently submitted, and Huangzhong governed with simplicity and ease until his jurisdiction was thoroughly well ordered.

sentences.zh: 一日，案行府署中，見一室扃鑰甚固，命發視之，得金寶數十匱，計直數百萬，乃李氏宮閣中遺物也，即表上之。

translations.literal: One day, while inspecting the prefectural offices on circuit, he saw a room locked very firmly. He ordered it opened and inspected; inside were several tens of chests of gold and jewels, reckoned worth several millions—these were relics left in the palace pavilion of the Li house. He immediately memorialized and presented them upward.
translations.idiomatic: One day, touring the prefectural offices, he found a room locked unusually tight. When he had it opened, he discovered dozens of chests of gold and jewels worth millions—the hoarded relics of the Li palace—and at once reported them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上覽表謂侍臣曰：「非黃中廉恪，則亡國之寶，將汙法而害人矣。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and said to attending ministers: "Had it not been for Huangzhong's integrity and restraint, the treasures of a fallen state would have stained the law and harmed people."
translations.idiomatic: Reading the memorial, the emperor told his attendants, "Had Huangzhong not been so upright and restrained, the treasures of a fallen dynasty would have corrupted the law and harmed the people."

sentences.zh: 」賜錢三十萬。

translations.literal: He was granted three hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong was rewarded with three hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，起復視事。

translations.literal: When his father died he entered mourning, then was recalled from mourning to resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he entered mourning, then was recalled to office before the mourning period ended.

sentences.zh: 五年，召歸闕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was summoned back to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was summoned back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 有薦黃中文學高第，召試中書，拜駕部員外郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: Someone recommended Huangzhong for high standing in letters and learning. He was summoned to examination in the Secretariat and appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of War's Chariots Section and Drafter of Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When someone recommended Huangzhong for outstanding literary learning, he was examined in the Secretariat and appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of War's Chariots Section with duty drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 八年，與宋白、呂蒙正等同知貢舉，遷司封郎中，充翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, together with Song Bai, Lü Mengzheng, and others he jointly supervised the tribute examination. He was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Rites' Seals Section and filled the post of Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he served with Song Bai, Lü Mengzheng, and others as co-supervisor of the civil examinations, was made Director in the Ministry of Rites' Seals Section, and appointed Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，又知貢舉，俄掌吏部選。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he again supervised the tribute examination and soon took charge of selections in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Yongxi era he again supervised the examinations and soon took charge of appointments in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，加中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was added as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Duangong era he was additionally appointed Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 二年，兼史館修撰。

translations.literal: In the second year he was concurrently made Compiler in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was also made compiler in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 凡再典貢部，多柬拔寒俊，除擬官吏，品藻精當。

translations.literal: In all he twice presided over the tribute department, largely selecting and elevating talented men of humble background. In appointing and proposing officials, his evaluations were precise and apt.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he presided over the examinations and largely advanced talented men of humble origin. In recommending officials his judgments were consistently apt.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年秋，與李沆並拜給事中、參知政事。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Chunhua he and Li Hang were together appointed Supervising Attendant and Participant in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the second year of the Chunhua era he and Li Hang were jointly appointed Supervising Attendant and Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 太宗召見其母王氏，命坐，謂曰：「教子如是，真孟母矣。

translations.literal: Taizong summoned his mother, Lady Wang, ordered her to sit, and said: "To teach a son thus is truly to be a Mencius's mother."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong summoned his mother, Lady Wang, had her seated, and said, "To raise a son like this is truly the work of Mencius's mother."

sentences.zh: 」作詩以賜之，頒賜甚厚。

translations.literal: He composed a poem and bestowed it on her, with distributions and gifts very generous.
translations.idiomatic: He composed a poem for her and bestowed lavish gifts besides.

sentences.zh: 黃中素重呂端為人，屬端出鎮襄陽，黃中力薦於上，因留為樞密直學士，遂參知政事。

translations.literal: Huangzhong had always valued Lü Duan's character. When Duan was to go out to guard Xiangyang, Huangzhong strongly recommended him to the emperor, and thereby Duan was kept as Academician Direct in the Bureau of Military Affairs and then became Participant in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong had long admired Lü Duan's character. When Duan was posted to guard Xiangyang, Huangzhong strongly recommended him to the throne, and Duan was kept at court as direct academician in the Bureau of Military Affairs and later made Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 當世文行之士，多黃中所薦引，而未嘗言，人莫之知也。

translations.literal: Men of letters and conduct in his age were largely introduced through Huangzhong's recommendation, yet he never spoke of it, and people did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Many leading scholars and men of integrity of the age owed their advancement to Huangzhong, yet he never spoke of it, and few knew.

sentences.zh: 然畏慎過甚，中書政事頗留不決。

translations.literal: Yet he was overly fearful and cautious, and affairs of the Secretariat often remained undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was excessively cautious, and Secretariat business often lingered unresolved.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，與沆並罷守本官。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year he and Hang were together dismissed and kept their original offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year he and Li Hang were dismissed together and retained only their original ranks.

sentences.zh: 明年，知襄州，上言母老乞留京，改知澶州。

translations.literal: The next year he administered Xiang Prefecture. He memorialized that his mother was old and begged to remain in the capital; he was changed to administer Chan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made prefect of Xiangzhou, but memorialized that his mother was elderly and begged to remain near the capital; he was reassigned to Chanzhou instead.

sentences.zh: 辭日，上戒之曰：「夫小心翼翼，君臣皆當然；

translations.literal: On the day of his farewell audience the emperor admonished him, saying: "To be cautious and fearful in small matters—this is proper for both ruler and minister;
translations.idiomatic: On the day he took leave, the emperor admonished him, saying, "Caution in small things is proper for ruler and subject alike;

sentences.zh: 若太過，則失大臣之體。

translations.literal: but if it goes too far, one loses the bearing proper to a great minister."
translations.idiomatic: but taken too far it ceases to suit a great minister."

sentences.zh: 」黃中頓首謝。

translations.literal: Huangzhong bowed his head to the ground in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong kowtowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 上因謂侍臣曰：「朕嘗念其母有賢德，七十餘年未覺老，每與之語，甚明敏。

translations.literal: The emperor then said to attending ministers: "I have often reflected that his mother possesses worthy virtue. Though over seventy, one does not sense age in her. Whenever I speak with her, she is very clear and keen."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then told his attendants, "I have often thought how worthy his mother is. Though past seventy, she seems scarcely aged, and whenever I speak with her she is remarkably sharp."

sentences.zh: 黃中終日憂畏，必先其母老矣。

translations.literal: Huangzhong is anxious and fearful all day long—surely he anticipates his mother's old age.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong lives in constant anxiety—no doubt because he fears for his aging mother."

sentences.zh: 」因目參知政事蘇易簡曰：「易簡之母亦如之。

translations.literal: " He then looked at Participant in Governance Su Yijian and said: "Yijian's mother is likewise so."
translations.idiomatic: " He then looked at Vice Grand Councilor Su Yijian and said, "Yijian's mother is the same."

sentences.zh: 自古賢母不可多得。

translations.literal: From antiquity worthy mothers have been hard to obtain in great number.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy mothers have always been rare.

sentences.zh: 」易簡前謝曰：「陛下以孝治天下，獎及人親，臣實何人，膺茲榮遇。」

translations.literal: Yijian stepped forward in thanks and said: "Your Majesty governs the realm through filial piety and extends reward even to others' parents. What sort of person is your servant to receive such honored favor?"
translations.idiomatic: Yijian stepped forward and replied, "Your Majesty governs the realm through filial piety and honors even others' parents. What am I, that I should receive such grace?"

sentences.zh: 至道初，黃中遘疾，詔令歸闕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhidao, Huangzhong fell ill and was ordered by edict to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhidao era Huangzhong fell ill, and an edict ordered him back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 會建儲宮，擇大臣有德望者為賓友，黃中在選中。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent's palace was being established, major ministers of virtue and standing were chosen as his companions in study; Huangzhong was among those selected.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent's household was established, eminent ministers were chosen as his tutors, and Huangzhong was among them.

sentences.zh: 以久疾，改命李至、李沆兼賓客，黃中亦特拜禮部侍郎，代至兼秘書監。

translations.literal: Because of long illness, the appointment was changed to Li Zhi and Li Hang jointly serving as companions. Huangzhong was also specially appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, replacing Zhi while concurrently holding Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his prolonged illness, Li Zhi and Li Hang were appointed joint tutors instead. Huangzhong was specially made Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and replaced Zhi as concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 黃中素嗜文籍，既居內閣，甚以為慰。

translations.literal: Huangzhong had always loved literary works. Once he held office in the inner cabinet, he found it a great consolation.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong had always loved books, and once he held office in the inner cabinet he found the post a great comfort.

sentences.zh: 二年，以疾卒，年五十六，其母尚無恙，卒如上言。

translations.literal: In the second year he died of illness, aged fifty-six. His mother was still without ailment, and he died just as he had spoken earlier.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he died of illness at fifty-six. His mother was still in good health, and he died as he had foretold.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 上聞其素貧，別賜錢三十萬。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that he had always been poor and separately granted three hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that he had always been poor, the emperor granted him an additional three hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 既葬，其母入謝，又賜白金三百兩。

translations.literal: After the burial his mother entered to give thanks, and she was again granted three hundred taels of white metal.
translations.idiomatic: After the funeral his mother came to court to give thanks and received another three hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 上謂之曰：「勿以諸孫為念，朕當不忘也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to her: "Do not worry over your grandsons; I shall not forget them."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told her, "Do not worry for your grandsons; I shall not forget them."

sentences.zh: 黃中端謹，能守家法，廉白無私。

translations.literal: Huangzhong was proper and cautious, able to uphold his family's standards, upright and white without selfishness.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhong was decorous and disciplined, upheld his family's standards, and was scrupulously honest and impartial.

sentences.zh: 多知臺閣故事，談論亹亹，聽者忘倦焉。

translations.literal: He knew many precedents of the terrace pavilions. His discourse flowed unceasingly, and listeners forgot weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He knew a great store of court precedent and could talk at length without wearying his listeners.

sentences.zh: 在翰林日，太宗召見，訪以時政得失，黃中但言：「臣職典書詔，思不出位，軍國政事，非臣所知。

translations.literal: While in the Hanlin Academy, Taizong summoned him and inquired about the gains and losses of current policy. Huangzhong only said: "Your servant's duty is to oversee edicts and decrees. My thoughts do not go beyond my office. Military and state affairs are not what your servant knows."
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the Hanlin Academy, Emperor Taizong summoned him and asked about current policy. Huangzhong replied only, "My duty is to draft edicts; my thoughts do not stray beyond my office. Military and state affairs are not for me to judge."

sentences.zh: 」上益重之，以為謹厚。

translations.literal: The emperor valued him all the more and regarded him as cautious and solid.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued him all the more for his restraint and integrity.

sentences.zh: 及知政事，卒無所建明，時論不之許。

translations.literal: When he came to know state affairs, in the end he made no clarifying proposals, and contemporary opinion did not approve him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he entered the chief council, however, he offered no notable initiatives, and contemporary opinion did not regard him favorably.

sentences.zh: 有文集三十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 子守謙，雍熙二年進士；

translations.literal: His son Shouqian passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Yongxi;
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouqian passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Yongxi era;

sentences.zh: 守正，獻文召試，賜進士第，後為虞部員外郎；

translations.literal: Shouzheng, through presenting a literary work, was summoned to examination and granted jinshi rank, later becoming Vice Director of the Ministry of War's Chariots Section;
translations.idiomatic: Shouzheng, after submitting a literary work for examination, was granted jinshi status and later became Vice Director in the Ministry of War's Chariots Section;

sentences.zh: 守約，國子博士；

translations.literal: Shouyue, Erudite of the Directorate of Education;
translations.idiomatic: Shouyue, Erudite of the Directorate of Education;

sentences.zh: 守文，殿中丞；

translations.literal: Shouwen, Director Within the Hall;
translations.idiomatic: Shouwen, Director Within the Hall;

sentences.zh: 守訥，右讚善大夫。

translations.literal: Shoune, Right Mentor Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Shoune, Right Mentor Grandee.

sentences.zh: 論曰：《詩》云：「允也天子，降予卿士，實為阿衡，實左右商王。

translations.literal: The commentary says: The Book of Songs states: "Truly is the Son of Heaven; he sends down to us ministers and grandees, who truly serve as Chief Regulator and truly assist and flank the King of Shang."
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: The Book of Songs declares, "Surely the Son of Heaven sends down ministers and grandees to serve as Chief Regulator and to stand at the side of the King of Shang."

sentences.zh: 」言有是君則有是臣，有是臣則足以相是君也。

translations.literal: This means that where there is such a lord, there are such ministers; where there are such ministers, they suffice to assist such a lord.
translations.idiomatic: This means that such a ruler draws forth such ministers, and such ministers are fit to assist such a ruler.

sentences.zh: 太宗勵精庶政，注意輔相，以昉舊德，亟加進用，繼擢蒙正、齊賢，迭居相位；

translations.literal: Taizong exerted himself in the myriad affairs of government and paid close attention to assisting ministers. Because of Fang's old virtue he was quickly advanced in employment; Mengzheng and Qixian were next promoted and in turn held the phase position;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong threw himself into governance and chose his chief ministers with care. He quickly advanced Li Fang for his long service, then raised Lü Mengzheng and Zhang Qixian in turn to the chief ministership;

sentences.zh: 復進黃中，俾參大政。

translations.literal: Huangzhong was again advanced and made to participate in great affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: and later advanced Jia Huangzhong to share in high policy.

sentences.zh: 而四臣者將順德美，修明庶政，以致承平之治，可謂君臣各盡其道者矣。

translations.literal: These four ministers followed and complied with virtuous excellence, clarified and brightened the myriad affairs of government, and thereby brought about the governance of sustained peace. It may be said that ruler and ministers each fulfilled their proper paths.
translations.idiomatic: These four ministers followed their sovereign's virtue, refined ordinary administration, and helped bring about an age of peace—a case in which ruler and ministers each fulfilled their proper roles.

sentences.zh: 君子謂李昉為多遜所毀而不校，蒙正為張紳所汙而不辨，齊賢為同列所累而不言，黃中多所薦引而不有其功，此固人之所難也。

translations.literal: Men of worth said that Li Fang was slandered by Duoxun yet did not contend; Mengzheng was defiled by Zhang Shen yet did not argue; Qixian was implicated by colleagues yet did not speak; Huangzhong introduced many men yet did not claim the merit—these are indeed what people find hard.
translations.idiomatic: Men of judgment observed that Li Fang was slandered by Li Duoxun yet did not answer back, that Lü Mengzheng was maligned by Zhang Shen yet did not defend himself, that Zhang Qixian was burdened by colleagues yet kept silent, and that Jia Huangzhong advanced many men yet claimed no credit—qualities that are genuinely hard to achieve.

sentences.zh: 而況四臣者皆賢宰輔，又能進退有禮，皆以善終，非盛德君子，其孰能與於斯？

translations.literal: Moreover, these four ministers were all worthy chief assistants, and were also able to advance and withdraw with propriety, all ending well. Had they not been gentlemen of abundant virtue, who could have joined in this?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, all four were worthy chief ministers who advanced and withdrew with propriety and ended their lives well. Without men of great virtue, who could have matched them?
